library_course_instructor_normalized.name: library_course_instructor_normalized
library_course_instructor_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- primary key carried through
  lci.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY,

  -- raw course name as provided
  lci.COURSE_NAME,

  -- normalized course name: trim, collapse internal spaces, uppercase,
  -- remove punctuation commonly interfering with joins, and keep numeric parts
  UPPER(
    TRIM(
      REGEXP_REPLACE(
        REGEXP_REPLACE(lci.COURSE_NAME, '[[:punct:]]', ' '),    -- replace punctuation with space
        '\\s+', ' '                                             -- collapse multiple spaces to single
      )
    )
  ) AS COURSE_NAME_NORMALIZED,

  -- raw instructor name as provided
  lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME,

  -- normalized instructor name: trim, collapse spaces, uppercase,
  -- remove punctuation, remove titles (Dr, Prof, Mr, Mrs, Ms) for better matching
  UPPER(
    TRIM(
      REGEXP_REPLACE(
        REGEXP_REPLACE(
          REGEXP_REPLACE(lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME, '(?i)\\b(DR|PROF|PROFESSOR|MR|MRS|MS)\\.?\\b', ' '), -- remove common titles
          '[[:punct:]]', ' '                                                          -- replace punctuation
        ),
        '\\s+', ' '
      )
    )
  ) AS INSTRUCTOR_NAME_NORMALIZED,

  -- department and unit carried through (trimmed)
  TRIM(lci.DEPARTMENT) AS DEPARTMENT,
  TRIM(lci.UNIT) AS UNIT,

  -- date range fields: keep as-is but trimmed; consumers can parse further
  TRIM(lci.DATE_FROM) AS DATE_FROM,
  TRIM(lci.DATE_TO) AS DATE_TO

FROM library_course_instructor lci
library_course_instructor_normalized.description: One row per library course instructor occurrence with canonicalized course and instructor fields to support joins to subject/course tables. Cleans/trims course and instructor names (keeps raw values too) so downstream joins can match on SUBJECT_ID or MASTER_SUBJECT_ID or title.

fac_building_with_room_metrics.name: fac_building_with_room_metrics
fac_building_with_room_metrics.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.`FAC_BUILDING_KEY` AS `FCLT_BUILDING_KEY`,
  b.`BUILDING_NAME` AS `BUILDING_NAME`,
  b.`BUILDING_NUMBER` AS `BUILDING_NUMBER`,
  b.`DATE_BUILT` AS `DATE_BUILT`,
  COALESCE(room_aggr.`ROOM_COUNT`, 0) AS `ROOM_COUNT`,
  COALESCE(room_aggr.`TOTAL_AREA_SQFT`, 0) AS `TOTAL_AREA_SQFT`,
  -- NUM_EMPLOYEES_PROXY is a simple proxy: one employee per X square feet.
  -- The divisor is a literal and should be supplied/adjusted outside the view if needed.
  -- Here we use 150 sqft per employee as the proxy divisor lifted out as a literal.
  FLOOR(COALESCE(room_aggr.`TOTAL_AREA_SQFT`, 0) / 150) AS `NUM_EMPLOYEES_PROXY`
FROM
  fac_building b
LEFT JOIN (
  -- aggregated room metrics per building
  SELECT
    COALESCE(rb.`FAC_BUILDING_KEY`, rb.`BUILDING_NUMBER`) AS `FAC_BUILDING_KEY`,
    COUNT(*) AS `ROOM_COUNT`,
    -- prefer assignable area where available, else use ext gross area per-room if provided.
    SUM(COALESCE(rb.`ASSIGNABLE_AREA`, rb.`EXT_GROSS_AREA`, 0)) AS `TOTAL_AREA_SQFT`
  FROM
    fac_building rb
  -- rooms may be stored in a related table in some schemas; if there were a fac_room table
  -- you'd aggregate from that table instead. Here we conservatively treat fac_building rows
  -- that include NUM_OF_ROOMS and assignable area as proxies for room-level counts.
  GROUP BY
    COALESCE(rb.`FAC_BUILDING_KEY`, rb.`BUILDING_NUMBER`)
) room_aggr
  ON room_aggr.`FAC_BUILDING_KEY` = b.`FAC_BUILDING_KEY`
fac_building_with_room_metrics.description: Denormalized building-level relation by joining fclt_building to aggregated room metrics (one row per building) and exposing building name, raw DATE_BUILT, and room-based measures which can act as employee-count proxies.

iap_subject_detail_clean.name: iap_subject_detail_clean
iap_subject_detail_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical key for the iap subject category (carry through original if present)
  COALESCE(iap.`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY`, NULL) AS `IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY`,

  -- term code preserved as-is (lifted literal: none)
  iap.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,

  -- activity title trimmed; keep exact text as canonical ACTIVITY_TITLE
  TRIM(iap.`ACTIVITY_TITLE`) AS `ACTIVITY_TITLE`,

  -- FEE: normalized numeric cast. Accepts integers or numeric strings; empty or non-numeric -> NULL.
  -- remove currency symbols and commas, treat empty string as NULL
  CASE
    WHEN iap.`FEE` IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(iap.`FEE`) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE
      -- strip common non-numeric characters then cast; if cast fails produce NULL via NULLIF + +0 trick
      -- remove dollar sign and commas and parentheses for negative amounts
      CAST(
        NULLIF(
          REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(TRIM(iap.`FEE`), '$', ''), ',', ''), '(', '-'), ')', '')
        , '') AS DECIMAL(18,2)
      )
  END AS `FEE`,

  -- MAX_ENROLLMENT: integer normalized. Non-numeric or empty -> NULL.
  CASE
    WHEN iap.`MAX_ENROLLMENT` IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(iap.`MAX_ENROLLMENT`) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE
      CAST(
        NULLIF(
          -- remove any commas or non-digit trailing text (keep leading digits)
          REGEXP_SUBSTR(TRIM(iap.`MAX_ENROLLMENT`), '^[0-9]+')
        , '') AS SIGNED
      )
  END AS `MAX_ENROLLMENT`,

  -- ATTENDANCE: normalized text (canonical): trim and upper to reduce variants; empty -> NULL
  NULLIF( NULLIF( TRIM(iap.`ATTENDANCE`), '' ), '' ) AS `ATTENDANCE`

FROM
  -- base table for IAP subject details; use the table name as provided in schema if exists.
  -- The schema does not explicitly list an iap_subject_detail table in the DDL snippet, but the view is defined
  -- to be one row per iap_subject_category_key / term_code / activity_title. Assume source table name `iap_subject_detail`.
  `iap_subject_detail` AS iap
iap_subject_detail_clean.description: Normalized/cleaned row-level IAP subject records with numeric casts for fee and max enrollment and canonical keys. One row per iap_subject_detail record.

space_detail_room_level.name: space_detail_room_level
space_detail_room_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- building component (e.g., wing/section) if available, else building name as fallback
  COALESCE(sd.BUILDING_COMPONENT, b.BUILDING_NAME) AS `BUILDING_COMPONENT`,
  -- room square footage: prefer ROOM_SQUARE_FOOTAGE from space_detail, else use ASSIGNABLE_AREA if single-room building allocation
  sd.ROOM_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS `ROOM_SQUARE_FOOTAGE`,
  -- building_room: a human-friendly identifier combining building number and room number
  CONCAT(
    COALESCE(b.BUILDING_NUMBER, ''),
    CASE WHEN b.BUILDING_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND sd.ROOM_NUMBER IS NOT NULL THEN '-' WHEN b.BUILDING_NUMBER IS NULL AND sd.ROOM_NUMBER IS NOT NULL THEN '' ELSE '' END,
    COALESCE(sd.ROOM_NUMBER, '')
  ) AS `BUILDING_ROOM`,
  -- room number as stored on the space_detail record
  sd.ROOM_NUMBER AS `ROOM_NUMBER`,
  -- floor-level key to join to floor tables (if present)
  sd.FLOOR_KEY AS `FLOOR_KEY`,
  -- building key to join to fac_building / fac_building_base
  sd.BUILDING_KEY AS `BUILDING_KEY`,
  -- primary key for this room-level space_detail row
  sd.SPACE_UNIT_KEY AS `SPACE_UNIT_KEY`
FROM
  space_detail sd
LEFT JOIN
  fac_building b
    ON sd.BUILDING_KEY = b.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
space_detail_room_level.description: One row per space_detail entry (room-level), exposing building component, room square footage, room/floor identifiers and keys useful to join to facility room/building tables.

iap_subject_detail_core.name: iap_subject_detail_core
iap_subject_detail_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  iap.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY,
  iap.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY,
  iap.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY,
  iap.ACTIVITY_TITLE,
  iap.TERM_CODE,
  -- liftable literal: default max enrollment when unknown (use NULL by default; caller can replace)
  iap.MAX_ENROLLMENT,
  -- normalized cancelled flag: keep original text but also coerce common values to 'Y'/'N'
  CASE
    WHEN iap.IS_CANCELLED IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN UPPER(TRIM(iap.IS_CANCELLED)) IN ('Y','YES','TRUE','1') THEN 'Y'
    WHEN UPPER(TRIM(iap.IS_CANCELLED)) IN ('N','NO','FALSE','0') THEN 'N'
    ELSE iap.IS_CANCELLED
  END AS IS_CANCELLED,
  -- determine whether offering spans multiple sessions: prefer explicit flag, else infer from session key pattern
  CASE
    WHEN iap.IS_MULTIPLE_SESSION IS NOT NULL THEN
      CASE
        WHEN UPPER(TRIM(iap.IS_MULTIPLE_SESSION)) IN ('Y','YES','TRUE','1') THEN 'Y'
        WHEN UPPER(TRIM(iap.IS_MULTIPLE_SESSION)) IN ('N','NO','FALSE','0') THEN 'N'
        ELSE iap.IS_MULTIPLE_SESSION
      END
    WHEN iap.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY IS NOT NULL AND iap.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY LIKE CONCAT('%', '-', '%') THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS IS_MULTIPLE_SESSION
FROM
  iap_subject_detail AS iap
iap_subject_detail_core.description: One row per IAP subject offering with its core descriptive fields and foreign-key keys to category, session, and sponsor.

sis_subject_code_core.name: sis_subject_code_core
sis_subject_code_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- department code as canonical join key to department-level tables
  COALESCE(ccs.DEPARTMENT_CODE, ccs.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,

  -- subject code is the SIS subject identifier used across catalogs
  COALESCE(ccs.SUBJECT_CODE, ccs.SUBJECT_CODE) AS SUBJECT_CODE,

  -- course number canonicalized (strip leading zeros and whitespace; keep original if null)
  NULLIF(TRIM(LEADING '0' FROM TRIM(ccs.SUBJECT_NUMBER)), '') AS COURSE_NUMBER,

  -- human-friendly subject/department description (prefer SUBJECT_TITLE then SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE then department)
  COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(ccs.SUBJECT_TITLE), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(ccs.SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(ccs.DEPARTMENT_NAME), '')) AS SUBJECT_CODE_DESC
FROM
  -- course catalog subject offered is the canonical SIS source for subjects + course number components
  course_catalog_subject_offered AS ccs
WHERE
  -- only include rows where we have a subject code and course number (grain requirement)
  ccs.SUBJECT_CODE IS NOT NULL
  AND ccs.SUBJECT_CODE <> ''
  AND ccs.SUBJECT_NUMBER IS NOT NULL
  AND ccs.SUBJECT_NUMBER <> ''
GROUP BY
  -- preserve grain: one row per SUBJECT_CODE, COURSE_NUMBER, DEPARTMENT_CODE
  COALESCE(ccs.DEPARTMENT_CODE, ccs.DEPARTMENT_CODE),
  COALESCE(ccs.SUBJECT_CODE, ccs.SUBJECT_CODE),
  NULLIF(TRIM(LEADING '0' FROM TRIM(ccs.SUBJECT_NUMBER)), '')
sis_subject_code_core.description: One row per SIS subject code with its department link and course number components; canonicalizes key columns used to join to course description and course-level tables.

sis_course_description_canonical.name: sis_course_description_canonical
sis_course_description_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical course identifier: prefer any existing normalized course name if present,
  -- otherwise use the raw course name. Lift literal handling to callers; here we just pass through.
  COALESCE(lcin.COURSE_NAME_NORMALIZED, lcin.COURSE_NAME) AS `COURSE`,

  -- graduate-level preferred field: if there is a column/flag named GRADUATE_LEVEL use it;
  -- otherwise prefer the misspelled GRADAUTE_LEVEL. In source tables provided there is no direct
  -- graduate-level column; however requirement is to expose both columns and prefer GRADUATE_LEVEL.
  -- We synthesize by trying to pull a value from COURSE_NAME / COURSE_NAME_NORMALIZED via simple pattern
  -- detection for common grad markers ('GR' or 'GRAD' etc). This is a best-effort normalization
  -- when explicit fields are not available in the catalog tables listed in depends_on.
  CASE
    WHEN lcin.COURSE_NAME_NORMALIZED REGEXP '(GRAD|GRADUATE|GR\\b|^GR\\b|GRAD\\b)' THEN 'Y'
    WHEN lcin.COURSE_NAME REGEXP '(GRAD|GRADUATE|GR\\b|^GR\\b|GRAD\\b)' THEN 'Y'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS `GRADUATE_LEVEL`,

  -- preserve the legacy/misspelled field name as well; mirror the same logic but put into GRADAUTE_LEVEL.
  CASE
    WHEN lcin.COURSE_NAME_NORMALIZED REGEXP '(GRAD|GRADUATE|GR\\b|^GR\\b|GRAD\\b)' THEN 'Y'
    WHEN lcin.COURSE_NAME REGEXP '(GRAD|GRADUATE|GR\\b|^GR\\b|GRAD\\b)' THEN 'Y'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS `GRADAUTE_LEVEL`,

  -- department code / id from the normalized library course instructor source
  lcin.DEPARTMENT AS `DEPARTMENT`,

  -- department name/title if present in the source
  lcin.UNIT AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`
FROM
  -- canonical source for course normalization and department mapping
  library_course_instructor_normalized lcin
GROUP BY
  -- grain: one row per canonical COURSE
  COALESCE(lcin.COURSE_NAME_NORMALIZED, lcin.COURSE_NAME),
  -- include department fields in grouping so rows remain deterministic if multiple depts map to same course
  lcin.DEPARTMENT,
  lcin.UNIT
sis_course_description_canonical.description: Normalized course description rows keyed by a canonical COURSE identifier and exposing graduate-level fields (preferring GRADUATE_LEVEL, falling back to GRADAUTE_LEVEL). Also expose COURSE (identifier) to allow joins to subject+course combos (subject code + course number).

department_subject_course_counts.name: department_subject_course_counts
department_subject_course_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(cc.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`, dc.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`) AS `DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
  COALESCE(cc.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, dc.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`) AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  cc.`SUBJECT_CODE` AS `SUBJECT_CODE`,
  cc.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS `SUBJECT_CODE_DESC`,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(cc.`SUBJECT_CODE`, '||', COALESCE(cc.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`, ''))) AS `TOTAL_COURSES`
FROM
  (
    -- canonical subject-level course offerings sourced from subject/catalog tables
    SELECT
      co.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
      co.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
      co.`SUBJECT_CODE`,
      co.`SUBJECT_TITLE`,
      co.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`,
      co.`SECTION_ID`
    FROM course_catalog_subject_offered co
    WHERE co.`SUBJECT_CODE` IS NOT NULL
      AND co.`SECTION_ID` IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
      dc.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
      dc.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
      dc.`SUBJECT_CODE`,
      dc.`SUBJECT_TITLE`,
      dc.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`,
      dc.`SECTION_ID`
    FROM drupal_course_catalog dc
    WHERE dc.`SUBJECT_CODE` IS NOT NULL
      AND dc.`SECTION_ID` IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
      cis.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
      cis.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
      cis.`SUBJECT_CODE`,
      cis.`SUBJECT_TITLE`,
      cis.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`,
      cis.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS `SECTION_ID`
    FROM cis_course_catalog cis
    WHERE cis.`SUBJECT_CODE` IS NOT NULL
      AND cis.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` IS NOT NULL
  ) cc
LEFT JOIN (
  -- optional department-only rows to ensure department_name presence when missing on specific catalog rows
  SELECT DISTINCT
    `DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
    `DEPARTMENT_NAME`
  FROM course_catalog_subject_offered
  WHERE `DEPARTMENT_CODE` IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT
    `DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
    `DEPARTMENT_NAME`
  FROM drupal_course_catalog
  WHERE `DEPARTMENT_CODE` IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT
    `DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
    `DEPARTMENT_NAME`
  FROM cis_course_catalog
  WHERE `DEPARTMENT_CODE` IS NOT NULL
) dc
  ON dc.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` = cc.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`
GROUP BY
  COALESCE(cc.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`, dc.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`),
  COALESCE(cc.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, dc.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`),
  cc.`SUBJECT_CODE`,
  cc.`SUBJECT_TITLE`
department_subject_course_counts.description: Counts of distinct course identifiers by department and subject code, using subject-level catalog tables. Produces one row per department + subject_code with a raw TOTAL_COURSES measure (distinct subject+course combos).

academic_terms_base.name: academic_terms_base

fac_building_summary.name: fac_building_summary
fac_building_summary.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY,
  fb.BUILDING_NAME,
  fb.ASSIGNABLE_AREA,
  -- sum of room assignable areas for the building; NULL if no rooms recorded
  SUM(r.ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS ROOMS_ASSIGNABLE_SUM
FROM fac_building fb
LEFT JOIN (
  -- room-level table(s) are not present in schema; try to use fac_building_with_room_metrics if available
  -- fac_building_with_room_metrics exposes building-level aggregated room metrics; it may include TOTAL_AREA_SQFT
  -- If that view exists, it will provide TOTAL_AREA_SQFT which we treat as ROOMS_ASSIGNABLE_SUM.
  -- Otherwise this subquery will be empty and SUM(...) will yield NULL.
  SELECT
    FCLT_BUILDING_KEY,
    TOTAL_AREA_SQFT AS ASSIGNABLE_AREA
  FROM fac_building_with_room_metrics
) r ON r.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
GROUP BY
  fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY,
  fb.BUILDING_NAME,
  fb.ASSIGNABLE_AREA
fac_building_summary.description: One row per building (FAC_BUILDING_KEY) with the building's assignable area and optionally the sum of room areas by building for verification or fallback.

building_core.name: building_core
building_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical building key: prefer fac_building FAC_BUILDING_KEY, fall back to buildings.BUILDING_KEY
  COALESCE(fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY, b.BUILDING_KEY) AS BUILDING_KEY,
  -- canonical building number: prefer fac_building BUILDING_NUMBER, else buildings.BUILDING_NUMBER
  COALESCE(NULLIF(fb.BUILDING_NUMBER, ''), NULLIF(b.BUILDING_NUMBER, '')) AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  -- canonical short name: prefer buildings.BUILDING_NAME, else fac_building BUILDING_NAME
  COALESCE(NULLIF(b.BUILDING_NAME, ''), NULLIF(fb.BUILDING_NAME, '')) AS BUILDING_NAME,
  -- canonical long name: prefer fac_building.BUILDING_NAME_LONG, then fac_building.BUILDING_NAME, then buildings.BUILDING_NAME
  COALESCE(NULLIF(fb.BUILDING_NAME_LONG, ''), NULLIF(fb.BUILDING_NAME, ''), NULLIF(b.BUILDING_NAME, '')) AS BUILDING_NAME_LONG
FROM fac_building fb
  -- left join to buildings so every fac_building row is represented and we can pull names/numbers from either source
  LEFT JOIN buildings b
    ON ( (fb.BUILDING_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND fb.BUILDING_NUMBER <> '' AND b.BUILDING_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND b.BUILDING_NUMBER <> '' AND fb.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER)
         OR (fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY IS NOT NULL AND fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY <> '' AND b.BUILDING_KEY IS NOT NULL AND b.BUILDING_KEY <> '' AND fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY)
       )
-- include buildings that might not have a fac_building record: union them in
UNION
SELECT
  -- for buildings-only rows use buildings.BUILDING_KEY as canonical key
  b2.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  NULLIF(b2.BUILDING_NUMBER, '') AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  NULLIF(b2.BUILDING_NAME, '') AS BUILDING_NAME,
  NULLIF(b2.BUILDING_NAME, '') AS BUILDING_NAME_LONG
FROM buildings b2
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM fac_building fb2
  WHERE ( (fb2.BUILDING_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND fb2.BUILDING_NUMBER <> '' AND b2.BUILDING_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND b2.BUILDING_NUMBER <> '' AND fb2.BUILDING_NUMBER = b2.BUILDING_NUMBER)
          OR (fb2.FAC_BUILDING_KEY IS NOT NULL AND fb2.FAC_BUILDING_KEY <> '' AND b2.BUILDING_KEY IS NOT NULL AND b2.BUILDING_KEY <> '' AND fb2.FAC_BUILDING_KEY = b2.BUILDING_KEY)
        )
)
building_core.description: One row per building key with canonical building identifiers and names from fac_building and buildings. Use to join building-level attributes to room/floor data.

department_reference_with_phone_and_scho.name: department_reference_with_phone_and_school
department_reference_with_phone_and_scho.body_sql:
SELECT
  sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  sd.SCHOOL_NAME AS SCHOOL_NAME,
  -- assemble phone: if area code present (non-null and not empty) then concatenate "(area) number", else use number, else null
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(ad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE, '') <> '' AND COALESCE(ad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER, '') <> '' THEN
      CONCAT('(', TRIM(ad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE), ') ', TRIM(ad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER))
    WHEN COALESCE(ad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER, '') <> '' THEN
      TRIM(ad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS DEPARTMENT_PHONE
FROM
  -- source of department-level reference (sis_department-like). Use available tables that contain department fields:
  -- prefer sis_admin_department when present for phone; department name and school come from sis_department if available,
  -- but those tables are not listed in schema; however course catalogs contain department fields (drupal_course_catalog, cis_course_catalog, course_catalog_subject_offered).
  -- Use course_catalog_subject_offered as primary source of department_code/name/school (ACADEMIC_YEAR may vary); aggregate to one row per department_code.
  (
    SELECT
      COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(department_code), ''), NULL) AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
      -- pick the most common non-null department name for this code
      SUBSTRING_INDEX(
        GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT NULLIF(TRIM(department_name), '') ORDER BY NULL SEPARATOR '|||'),
        '|||', 1
      ) AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
      -- school name is not consistently present; attempt to derive from department_name (leave null if unknown)
      NULL AS SCHOOL_NAME
    FROM course_catalog_subject_offered
    WHERE COALESCE(TRIM(department_code), '') <> ''
    GROUP BY department_code
  ) AS sd
LEFT JOIN
  (
    -- administrative department table with phone info: try sis_admin_department-like sources.
    -- Use drupal_employee_directory and employee_directory are people tables; there is sis_admin_department not in schema.
    -- However cis_course_catalog and course_catalog_subject_offered sometimes include DEPARTMENT_PHONE fields in other schemas; none present.
    -- Fall back to attempting to read phone fields from course_catalog_subject_offered if they existed; since no direct phone column exists, produce empty result to preserve joinability.
    SELECT
      NULL AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
      NULL AS DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE,
      NULL AS DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER
    WHERE 1=0
  ) AS ad
  ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ad.DEPARTMENT_CODE
department_reference_with_phone_and_scho.description: Department-level reference: one row per sis_department.DEPARTMENT_CODE with department name, school name, and department phone assembled from sis_admin_department if available (concatenate DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE and DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER when area code present).

instructor_contact_canonical.name: instructor_contact_canonical
instructor_contact_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical MIT_ID: prefer opa_person_current (if present), then employee_directory, then drupal_employee_directory
  COALESCE(opa.MIT_ID, ed.MIT_ID, ded.MIT_ID) AS MIT_ID,
  -- canonical full name: prefer opa_person_current.FULL_NAME, then employee_directory.FULL_NAME, then drupal_employee_directory.FULL_NAME
  COALESCE(opa.FULL_NAME, ed.FULL_NAME, ded.FULL_NAME) AS FULL_NAME,
  -- canonical primary email: prefer opa_person_current.EMAIL_ADDRESS, then employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS, then drupal_employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS
  COALESCE(opa.EMAIL_ADDRESS, ed.EMAIL_ADDRESS, ded.EMAIL_ADDRESS) AS EMAIL_ADDRESS,
  -- indicate which table supplied the canonical contact (OPA, EMPLOYEE_DIRECTORY, DRUPAL). If none, NULL.
  CASE
    WHEN opa.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL OR opa.EMAIL_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL OR opa.FULL_NAME IS NOT NULL THEN 'opa_person_current'
    WHEN ed.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL OR ed.EMAIL_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL OR ed.FULL_NAME IS NOT NULL THEN 'employee_directory'
    WHEN ded.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL OR ded.EMAIL_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL OR ded.FULL_NAME IS NOT NULL THEN 'drupal_employee_directory'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS SOURCE_TABLE
FROM
  -- opa_person_current may not exist as a base table in the provided DDL but can be referenced if present in the DB.
  -- left joins ensure we preserve any MIT_ID from opa (primary) while allowing fallbacks from other sources.
  (SELECT
     MIT_ID,
     FULL_NAME,
     EMAIL_ADDRESS
   FROM opa_person_current
  ) AS opa
  -- join employee_directory on MIT_ID when available; also include rows where opa is null by full outer semantics emulated with UNION below
  LEFT JOIN employee_directory AS ed
    ON ed.MIT_ID = opa.MIT_ID
  LEFT JOIN drupal_employee_directory AS ded
    ON ded.MIT_ID = opa.MIT_ID

UNION

SELECT
  COALESCE(opa2.MIT_ID, ed2.MIT_ID, ded2.MIT_ID) AS MIT_ID,
  COALESCE(opa2.FULL_NAME, ed2.FULL_NAME, ded2.FULL_NAME) AS FULL_NAME,
  COALESCE(opa2.EMAIL_ADDRESS, ed2.EMAIL_ADDRESS, ded2.EMAIL_ADDRESS) AS EMAIL_ADDRESS,
  CASE
    WHEN opa2.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL OR opa2.EMAIL_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL OR opa2.FULL_NAME IS NOT NULL THEN 'opa_person_current'
    WHEN ed2.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL OR ed2.EMAIL_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL OR ed2.FULL_NAME IS NOT NULL THEN 'employee_directory'
    WHEN ded2.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL OR ded2.EMAIL_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL OR ded2.FULL_NAME IS NOT NULL THEN 'drupal_employee_directory'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS SOURCE_TABLE
FROM
  -- rows present in employee_directory but not in opa_person_current
  (SELECT
     ed.MIT_ID,
     ed.FULL_NAME,
     ed.EMAIL_ADDRESS
   FROM employee_directory AS ed
   LEFT JOIN opa_person_current AS opa_e ON opa_e.MIT_ID = ed.MIT_ID
   WHERE opa_e.MIT_ID IS NULL
  ) AS ed2
  LEFT JOIN opa_person_current AS opa2
    ON opa2.MIT_ID = ed2.MIT_ID
  LEFT JOIN drupal_employee_directory AS ded2
    ON ded2.MIT_ID = ed2.MIT_ID

UNION

SELECT
  COALESCE(opa3.MIT_ID, ed3.MIT_ID, ded3.MIT_ID) AS MIT_ID,
  COALESCE(opa3.FULL_NAME, ed3.FULL_NAME, ded3.FULL_NAME) AS FULL_NAME,
  COALESCE(opa3.EMAIL_ADDRESS, ed3.EMAIL_ADDRESS, ded3.EMAIL_ADDRESS) AS EMAIL_ADDRESS,
  CASE
    WHEN opa3.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL OR opa3.EMAIL_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL OR opa3.FULL_NAME IS NOT NULL THEN 'opa_person_current'
    WHEN ed3.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL OR ed3.EMAIL_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL OR ed3.FULL_NAME IS NOT NULL THEN 'employee_directory'
    WHEN ded3.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL OR ded3.EMAIL_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL OR ded3.FULL_NAME IS NOT NULL THEN 'drupal_employee_directory'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS SOURCE_TABLE
FROM
  -- rows present in drupal_employee_directory but not in opa_person_current or employee_directory
  (SELECT
     ded.MIT_ID,
     ded.FULL_NAME,
     ded.EMAIL_ADDRESS
   FROM drupal_employee_directory AS ded
   LEFT JOIN opa_person_current AS opa_d ON opa_d.MIT_ID = ded.MIT_ID
   LEFT JOIN employee_directory AS ed_d ON ed_d.MIT_ID = ded.MIT_ID
   WHERE opa_d.MIT_ID IS NULL AND ed_d.MIT_ID IS NULL
  ) AS ded3
  LEFT JOIN opa_person_current AS opa3
    ON opa3.MIT_ID = ded3.MIT_ID
  LEFT JOIN employee_directory AS ed3
    ON ed3.MIT_ID = ded3.MIT_ID
instructor_contact_canonical.description: Canonical instructor contact rows combining person id, full name, and primary email by preferring MIT_ID-based person records when available. This allows joining instructor id or name to an email address.

building_hr_occupancy_agg.name: building_hr_occupancy_agg
building_hr_occupancy_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  COALESCE(fb.BUILDING_NAME, fb.BUILDING_NAME_LONG, fb.BUILDING_NUMBER) AS BUILDING_NAME,
  -- sum only non-null EXT_GROSS_AREA
  SUM(CASE WHEN fb.EXT_GROSS_AREA IS NOT NULL THEN fb.EXT_GROSS_AREA ELSE 0 END) AS TOTAL_EXT_GROSS_AREA,
  -- sum only non-null ASSIGNABLE_AREA
  SUM(CASE WHEN fb.ASSIGNABLE_AREA IS NOT NULL THEN fb.ASSIGNABLE_AREA ELSE 0 END) AS TOTAL_ASSIGNABLE_AREA,
  -- average of ASSIGNABLE_AREA excluding NULLs (use NULLIF to avoid division by zero)
  (CASE
     WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN fb.ASSIGNABLE_AREA IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN NULL
     ELSE SUM(CASE WHEN fb.ASSIGNABLE_AREA IS NOT NULL THEN fb.ASSIGNABLE_AREA ELSE 0 END)
          / SUM(CASE WHEN fb.ASSIGNABLE_AREA IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
   END) AS AVG_ASSIGNABLE_AREA,
  -- aggregated distinct HR department names from cost center / cost collector mapping table(s)
  -- join to employee_directory or other HR table is not available in schema; use fac_building.COST_CENTER_CODE and COST_COLLECTOR_KEY
  -- collect distinct non-null department identifiers as a comma-separated list
  NULLIF(TRIM(BOTH ',' FROM GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT
     CASE
       WHEN COALESCE(fb.COST_COLLECTOR_KEY, fb.COST_CENTER_CODE) IS NOT NULL
         THEN COALESCE(fb.COST_COLLECTOR_KEY, fb.COST_CENTER_CODE)
       ELSE NULL
     END
     ORDER BY COALESCE(fb.COST_COLLECTOR_KEY, fb.COST_CENTER_CODE) SEPARATOR ',')), '') AS HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  -- include raw DATE_BUILT from fac_building (take any non-null if multiple rows per building)
  MAX(fb.DATE_BUILT) AS DATE_BUILT
FROM fac_building fb
GROUP BY fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY, COALESCE(fb.BUILDING_NAME, fb.BUILDING_NAME_LONG, fb.BUILDING_NUMBER)
building_hr_occupancy_agg.description: Aggregated measures per building (FAC_BUILDING_KEY): sums of EXT_GROSS_AREA and ASSIGNABLE_AREA and average assignable area across fac_building rows for that key, plus aggregated HR department names matched via cost center or cost collector. Rows where numeric area fields are NULL are excluded from numeric aggregates. HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME is returned as a comma-separated list (distinct). DATE_BUILT is included (raw), to be parsed in final query.

subject_offered_term_section.name: subject_offered_term_section
subject_offered_term_section.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.`TERM_CODE` AS TERM_CODE,
  so.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  so.`SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION` AS SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION,
  so.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME` AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  so.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID` AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  so.`MEET_PLACE` AS MEET_PLACE,
  -- ROOM: if MEET_PLACE encodes "BUILDING ROOM" separated by space or '#' try to extract trailing token; otherwise keep MEET_PLACE
  TRIM(
    CASE
      WHEN so.`MEET_PLACE` IS NULL OR so.`MEET_PLACE` = '' THEN NULL
      WHEN so.`MEET_PLACE` LIKE '%#%' THEN SUBSTRING_INDEX(so.`MEET_PLACE`, '#', -1)
      WHEN so.`MEET_PLACE` REGEXP '[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z0-9/-]+$' THEN
        TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(so.`MEET_PLACE`, ' ', -1))
      ELSE so.`MEET_PLACE`
    END
  ) AS ROOM,
  -- BUILDING_ROOM: combine building number (if available) with room
  NULLIF(
    TRIM(
      CONCAT(
        COALESCE(fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER`, ''),
        CASE WHEN fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER` IS NOT NULL AND fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER` <> '' AND (
             (so.`MEET_PLACE` IS NOT NULL AND so.`MEET_PLACE` <> '')
           ) THEN ' ' ELSE '' END,
        TRIM(
          CASE
            WHEN so.`MEET_PLACE` IS NULL OR so.`MEET_PLACE` = '' THEN ''
            WHEN so.`MEET_PLACE` LIKE '%#%' THEN SUBSTRING_INDEX(so.`MEET_PLACE`, '#', -1)
            WHEN so.`MEET_PLACE` REGEXP '[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z0-9/-]+$' THEN SUBSTRING_INDEX(so.`MEET_PLACE`, ' ', -1)
            ELSE so.`MEET_PLACE`
          END
        )
      )
    ), ''
  ) AS BUILDING_ROOM,
  -- FLOOR: best-effort parse: look for 'FL' or 'FL.' or single leading digit in room/place
  NULLIF(
    TRIM(
      CASE
        WHEN so.`MEET_PLACE` REGEXP '[Ff][Ll]\\.?[[:space:]]*[0-9]+' THEN
          REGEXP_SUBSTR(so.`MEET_PLACE`, '[Ff][Ll]\\.?[[:space:]]*[0-9]+')
        WHEN so.`MEET_PLACE` REGEXP '[[:space:]]+[0-9]{1,2}[[:space:]]*([A-Za-z]{0,2})?$' THEN
          REGEXP_SUBSTR(so.`MEET_PLACE`, '[[:space:]][0-9]{1,2}[[:space:]]*$')
        ELSE NULL
      END
    ), ''
  ) AS FLOOR,
  -- FORM_TYPE: prefer TERM_DURATION or TERM DURATION-ish field; fall back to IS_MASTER_SECTION/IS_LECTURE_SECTION mapping
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(so.`TERM_DURATION`, ''),
    CASE
      WHEN so.`IS_MASTER_SECTION` = 'Y' THEN 'MASTER'
      WHEN so.`IS_LECTURE_SECTION` = 'Y' THEN 'LECTURE'
      WHEN so.`IS_LAB_SECTION` = 'Y' THEN 'LAB'
      WHEN so.`IS_RECITATION_SECTION` = 'Y' THEN 'RECITATION'
      WHEN so.`IS_DESIGN_SECTION` = 'Y' THEN 'DESIGN'
      ELSE NULL
    END
  ) AS FORM_TYPE,
  -- Offer department code and name
  so.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
  so.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS OFFER_DEPT_NAME
FROM
  course_catalog_subject_offered so
LEFT JOIN fac_building fb
  ON fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER` = -- try to match building number from MEET_PLACE leading token if present
     CASE
       WHEN so.`MEET_PLACE` IS NULL THEN NULL
       WHEN so.`MEET_PLACE` LIKE '%#%' THEN NULL
       WHEN so.`MEET_PLACE` REGEXP '^[A-Za-z0-9]+' THEN REGEXP_SUBSTR(so.`MEET_PLACE`, '^[A-Za-z0-9]+')
       ELSE NULL
     END
subject_offered_term_section.description: One row per offered subject-section (a specific section/meeting of a subject) with term, subject, department, responsible faculty, meeting place/time and course-type fields. Useful as the primary cohort of offered classes for term-level subject queries.

subject_attribute_term_subject_row.name: subject_attribute_term_subject_row
subject_attribute_term_subject_row.body_sql:
SELECT
  co.`TERM_CODE` AS TERM_CODE,
  co.`SUBJECT_ID` AS SUBJECT_ID,
  co.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,

library_course_instructor_canonical.name: library_course_instructor_canonical
library_course_instructor_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.`LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY`,
  -- canonical course name: prefer cleaned COURSE_NAME then normalized if available
  COALESCE(NULLIF(n.`COURSE_NAME`, ''), n.`COURSE_NAME_NORMALIZED`) AS `COURSE_NAME`,
  -- canonical instructor name: prefer provided name then normalized
  COALESCE(NULLIF(n.`INSTRUCTOR_NAME`, ''), n.`INSTRUCTOR_NAME_NORMALIZED`) AS `INSTRUCTOR_NAME`,
  n.`DEPARTMENT`,
  -- unit preserved as-is from normalized source
  n.`UNIT`,
  -- date range preserved; if empty strings treat as NULL
  NULLIF(n.`DATE_FROM`, '') AS `DATE_FROM`,
  NULLIF(n.`DATE_TO`, '') AS `DATE_TO`,
  -- UNIT_CODE derived from UNIT when possible: take trailing token like "3.0 (Lec)" or just numeric part
  -- lift any literal parsing rules out of the view; here produce a best-effort normalized code
  NULLIF(
    TRIM(
      -- extract leading numeric (including decimal) from UNIT
      REGEXP_SUBSTR(n.`UNIT`, '^[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?')
    ),
    ''
  ) AS `UNIT_CODE`
FROM
  library_course_instructor_normalized n
library_course_instructor_canonical.description: Canonicalized course-instructor rows: one row per LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY with course name, instructor name, unit and term (if available) for consistent grouping and joins.

library_reserve_catalog_years.name: library_reserve_catalog_years
library_reserve_catalog_years.body_sql:
SELECT
  lrc.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY`,
  lrc.`CATALOG_YEAR` AS `CATALOG_YEAR`,
  -- attempt to parse a numeric year: trim whitespace, remove surrounding punctuation, then cast when it is a pure integer (optionally with + or -)
  CASE
    WHEN TRIM(lrc.`CATALOG_YEAR`) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(lrc.`CATALOG_YEAR`) RLIKE '^[+-]?[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(TRIM(lrc.`CATALOG_YEAR`) AS SIGNED)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS `CATALOG_YEAR_NUM`
FROM
  `library_reserve_catalog` lrc

One row per library_reserve_catalog.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY exposing CATALOG_YEAR as both raw and numeric (null if non-numeric) so min/max year computations can ignore non-numeric values.

SELECT

  (

  LEFT JOIN academic_terms_all AS ata

SELECT

moira_list_core.name: moira_list_core
moira_list_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY,
  m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME,
  -- canonicalize boolean-like flags to 'Y'/'N' (lift literals out of view: compare to 'Y' in queries)
  CASE
    WHEN m.IS_PUBLIC IN ('Y','y','1','t','true','TRUE') THEN 'Y'
    WHEN m.IS_PUBLIC IS NULL THEN 'N'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS IS_PUBLIC,
  CASE
    WHEN m.IS_HIDDEN IN ('Y','y','1','t','true','TRUE') THEN 'Y'
    WHEN m.IS_HIDDEN IS NULL THEN 'N'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS IS_HIDDEN
FROM moira_list m
GROUP BY
  m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY,
  m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME,
  -- include the raw flag expressions used above so grouping is deterministic
  CASE
    WHEN m.IS_PUBLIC IN ('Y','y','1','t','true','TRUE') THEN 'Y'
    WHEN m.IS_PUBLIC IS NULL THEN 'N'
    ELSE 'N'
  END,
  CASE
    WHEN m.IS_HIDDEN IN ('Y','y','1','t','true','TRUE') THEN 'Y'
    WHEN m.IS_HIDDEN IS NULL THEN 'N'
    ELSE 'N'
  END

summer_teaching_records_by_person.name: summer_teaching_records_by_person
summer_teaching_records_by_person.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- person identifier carried through
  t.MIT_ID,
  -- source term code as stored in source table (keep original)
  t.TERM_CODE,
  -- normalized term year extracted from TERM_CODE:
  -- lift literal out: term suffix for summer is 'SU' (callers can change)
  -- TERM_YEAR: take TERM_CODE without trailing non-numeric SU part.
  CASE
    WHEN t.TERM_CODE RLIKE '^[0-9]{4}SU$' THEN LEFT(t.TERM_CODE,4)
    WHEN t.TERM_CODE RLIKE '^[0-9]{6}SU$' THEN LEFT(t.TERM_CODE,4) -- defend longer codes (take leading year)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS TERM_YEAR,
  -- which source table this row came from
  t.source_table,
  -- key/id in the source table for joinability back to source
  t.source_key
FROM (
  -- union all canonical teaching-related sources, each subselect must output MIT_ID, TERM_CODE, source_table, source_key
  -- 1) course instructors table: assume instructor MIT_ID is in RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID in course_catalog_subject_offered or drupal_course_catalog
  SELECT
    cs.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID AS MIT_ID,
    cs.TERM_CODE,
    'course_catalog_subject_offered' AS source_table,
    cs.SECTION_ID AS source_key
  FROM course_catalog_subject_offered cs
  WHERE cs.TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL
    AND cs.TERM_CODE LIKE CONCAT('%', 'SU') -- lift literal 'SU' out of view as needed

  UNION ALL

  -- 2) drupal_course_catalog responsible faculty
  SELECT
    d.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID AS MIT_ID,
    d.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
    'drupal_course_catalog' AS source_table,
    d.SECTION_ID AS source_key
  FROM drupal_course_catalog d
  WHERE d.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL
    AND d.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE LIKE CONCAT('%', 'SU')

  UNION ALL

  -- 3) iap_person_roles: roles during IAP may include instructors; use PERSON_EMAIL or PERSON_ORGANIZATION not ideal for MIT_ID.
  -- Here we assume PERSON_ROLE rows include a MIT_ID-like PERSON_NAME field when available in PERSON_EMAIL as localpart; best-effort: treat PERSON_EMAIL localpart as MIT_ID when email ends with '@mit.edu'
  SELECT
    SUBSTRING_INDEX(pr.PERSON_EMAIL, '@', 1) AS MIT_ID,
    pr.PERSON_ROLE AS TERM_CODE, -- PERSON_ROLE isn't a term; preserve as TERM_CODE only if it looks like a term code
    'iap_person_roles' AS source_table,
    pr.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY AS source_key
  FROM iap_person_roles pr
  WHERE pr.PERSON_EMAIL IS NOT NULL
    AND pr.PERSON_EMAIL LIKE '%@mit.edu'
    AND (pr.PERSON_ROLE IS NOT NULL AND pr.PERSON_ROLE LIKE CONCAT('%', 'SU'))


  UNION ALL

  -- 4) library_course_instructor_normalized: use DATE_FROM/DATE_TO to infer term codes if present in COURSE_NAME or DATE_FROM string; best-effort: use COURSE_NAME to find a TERM_CODE-like token ending with SU
  SELECT
    -- attempt to extract MIT_ID from INSTRUCTOR_NAME if formatted 'Last, First (mitid)' not guaranteed; keep as NULLable MIT_ID for callers to filter
    NULL AS MIT_ID,
    -- try to extract a TERM_CODE token from COURSE_NAME using simple pattern: four digits + SU
    CASE
      WHEN l.COURSE_NAME RLIKE '[0-9]{4}SU' THEN SUBSTRING(l.COURSE_NAME, REGEXP_INSTR(l.COURSE_NAME, '[0-9]{4}SU'), 6)
      ELSE NULL
    END AS TERM_CODE,
    'library_course_instructor_normalized' AS source_table,
    l.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY AS source_key
  FROM library_course_instructor_normalized l
  WHERE l.COURSE_NAME RLIKE '[0-9]{4}SU'


  UNION ALL

  -- 5) tip_subject_material_link: has TERM_CODE and SUBJECT_ID; instructor/person not directly present, but we include SUBJECT_ID in source_key to let callers join to person if available elsewhere
  SELECT
    NULL AS MIT_ID,
    tsm.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
    'tip_subject_material_link' AS source_table,
    tsm.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY AS source_key
  FROM tip_subject_material_link tsm
  WHERE tsm.TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL
    AND tsm.TERM_CODE LIKE CONCAT('%', 'SU')

) AS t
-- only keep rows where TERM_CODE ends with summer suffix 'SU' and MIT_ID is present (since grain requires MIT_ID)
WHERE t.TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL
  AND t.TERM_CODE LIKE CONCAT('%', 'SU')
  AND t.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL
summer_teaching_records_by_person.description: Canonical set of teaching-related records per person (MIT_ID) for terms whose TERM_CODE ends with 'SU'. Normalizes TERM_CODE for year extraction and exposes source table + term for each teaching instance so callers can filter by term-year or source.

building_keys_with_names.name: building_keys_with_names
building_keys_with_names.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- prefer canonical fac_building key, fall back to buildings.BUILDING_KEY when fac_building missing
  COALESCE(f.FAC_BUILDING_KEY, b.BUILDING_KEY) AS BUILDING_KEY,
  -- prefer fac_building BUILDING_NUMBER, then fac_building.BUILDING_NUMBER (both same name in sources),
  -- then buildings.BUILDING_NUMBER
  COALESCE(f.BUILDING_NUMBER, fb.BUILDING_NUMBER, b.BUILDING_NUMBER) AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  -- prefer fac_building BUILDING_NAME (long form), then fac_building.BUILDING_NAME, then buildings.BUILDING_NAME
  COALESCE(f.BUILDING_NAME, fb.BUILDING_NAME, b.BUILDING_NAME) AS BUILDING_NAME
FROM
  -- fac_building may contain richer canonical building keys; alias as f
  fac_building AS f
  -- join to fac_building_base view if available to pull its BUILDING_NAME/NUMBER (depends_on list allows it).
  LEFT JOIN fac_building_base AS fb
    ON f.FAC_BUILDING_KEY = fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY
  -- also left join the older buildings table to pick up any keys/numbers/names that only exist there
  LEFT JOIN buildings AS b
    ON (
      -- join on explicit building number when available
      (f.BUILDING_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND f.BUILDING_NUMBER <> '' AND b.BUILDING_NUMBER = f.BUILDING_NUMBER)
      OR
      -- fall back to matching by building name if number not present
      ( (f.BUILDING_NUMBER IS NULL OR f.BUILDING_NUMBER = '') AND b.BUILDING_NAME IS NOT NULL AND b.BUILDING_NAME <> '' AND b.BUILDING_NAME = f.BUILDING_NAME )
    )

UNION

-- include buildings rows that have no matching fac_building (so one row per BUILDING_KEY overall)
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME
FROM buildings b
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM fac_building f2
  WHERE
    -- consider a fac_building that refers to same building by number or name as matching
    (f2.BUILDING_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND f2.BUILDING_NUMBER <> '' AND f2.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER)
    OR
    ( (f2.BUILDING_NUMBER IS NULL OR f2.BUILDING_NUMBER = '') AND f2.BUILDING_NAME IS NOT NULL AND f2.BUILDING_NAME <> '' AND f2.BUILDING_NAME = b.BUILDING_NAME)
)
building_keys_with_names.description: Canonical mapping of building key to building number and building name by consolidating fac_building and buildings tables. One row per building key. Allows joining building keys to human-readable building names and building numbers used in office locations.

moira_list_faculty_members.name: moira_list_faculty_members
moira_list_faculty_members.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY,
  m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME,
  md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER,
  -- canonicalize member full name: prefer detail full name if present, else use member text
  COALESCE(NULLIF(md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_FULL_NAME, ''), md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER) AS MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_FULL_NAME,
  -- resolved MIT ID: prefer explicit MIT id on detail, else try to match faculty by name (will be the matched FACULTY_MIT_ID)
  NULLIF(md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID, '') AS MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID_resolved,
  -- faculty columns (may be NULL if not matched)
  f.MIT_ID AS FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  f.FULL_NAME AS FACULTY_FULL_NAME,
  f.LAST_NAME AS FACULTY_LAST_NAME,
  -- is_faculty_flag: 1 if member is identified as faculty either by explicit MIT id matching faculty table
  -- or by name match to faculty roster; 0 otherwise
  CASE
    WHEN (NULLIF(md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID, '') IS NOT NULL AND NULLIF(md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID, '') = f.MIT_ID) THEN 1
    WHEN f.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS is_faculty_flag
FROM moira_list AS m
JOIN moira_list_detail AS md
  ON md.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
LEFT JOIN employee_directory AS f
  -- first try to match by explicit MIT ID on the moira member detail
  ON (
       (NULLIF(md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID, '') IS NOT NULL AND f.MIT_ID = NULLIF(md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID, ''))
     )
LEFT JOIN (
  -- name-based faculty match: try to match member text to employee full name or last/first combinations.
  -- This derived table finds a faculty row when the moira member text equals or contains the faculty name pieces.
  SELECT ed.MIT_ID, ed.FULL_NAME, ed.LAST_NAME
  FROM employee_directory ed
) AS fname
  ON (
       -- only use name-match when there wasn't already an explicit MIT ID match to 'f' above
       (NULLIF(md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID, '') IS NULL)
       AND (
            -- exact full name match (case-insensitive)
            LOWER(NULLIF(md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_FULL_NAME, '')) = LOWER(fname.FULL_NAME)
            OR LOWER(md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER) = LOWER(fname.FULL_NAME)
            -- or member string contains "<last>, <first>" or "<first> <last>"
            OR (fname.LAST_NAME IS NOT NULL AND LOWER(md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER) LIKE CONCAT('%', LOWER(fname.LAST_NAME), '%'))
       )
     )
-- prefer explicit MIT-ID join result when present; otherwise pull name-match faculty info into f columns
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    /* pass-through to allow COALESCE choice between explicit-id join (f) and name-match (fname) */
    /* no rows here; this alias is used only to enable COALESCE logic below when f is null */
    NULL AS MIT_ID, NULL AS FULL_NAME, NULL AS LAST_NAME
) AS filler ON 1=0
moira_list_faculty_members.description: One row per mailing-list member that is identified as a faculty person by MIT_ID or by name-match to faculty rosters. Normalizes member identity to a resolved MIT_ID and canonical full/last/first name when available.

SELECT

subject_codes_by_department.name: subject_codes_by_department
subject_codes_by_department.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  c.`SUBJECT_CODE` AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  -- prefer subject/title from course_catalog_subject_offered if present, fall back to cis_course_catalog or drupal_course_catalog
  COALESCE(ccso.SUBJECT_TITLE, cis.SUBJECT_TITLE, drupal.SUBJECT_TITLE) AS SUBJECT_CODE_DESC,
  -- derive school code/name from department_code prefix or from department_name where available
  -- Lifted literals: none hard-coded; logic only uses available columns
  -- SCHOOL_CODE: take left 2 characters of DEPARTMENT_CODE if department code present
  CASE
    WHEN c.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` IS NOT NULL AND c.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` <> '' THEN LEFT(c.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`, 2)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS SCHOOL_CODE,
  -- SCHOOL_NAME: prefer department name from course_catalog_subject_offered, fall back to cis or drupal department name
  COALESCE(c.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, cis.DEPARTMENT_NAME, drupal.DEPARTMENT_NAME) AS SCHOOL_NAME
FROM
  course_catalog_subject_offered c
  LEFT JOIN cis_course_catalog cis
    ON c.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL
    AND cis.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = c.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
    -- also try matching subject_code/subject_id if MASTER_SUBJECT_ID not reliable
  LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog drupal
    ON (c.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL AND drupal.SUBJECT_ID = c.SUBJECT_ID)
  LEFT JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered ccso
    ON ccso.SUBJECT_ID = c.SUBJECT_ID
    AND ccso.TERM_CODE = c.TERM_CODE
WHERE
  -- only include rows that have a subject code and department code (grain)
  c.SUBJECT_CODE IS NOT NULL
  AND c.SUBJECT_CODE <> ''
  AND c.DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL
  AND c.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> ''
GROUP BY
  c.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  c.SUBJECT_CODE,
  SUBJECT_CODE_DESC,
  SCHOOL_CODE,
  SCHOOL_NAME

departments_per_school_agg_prep.name: departments_per_school_agg_prep
departments_per_school_agg_prep.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- department identifier (grain)
  COALESCE(ctso.DEPARTMENT_CODE, dcc.DEPARTMENT_CODE, dccf.DEPARTMENT_NUMBER) AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  -- school name / department grouping; prefer explicit department name fields, fall back to other available descriptors
  COALESCE(ctso.DEPARTMENT_NAME,
           dcc.DEPARTMENT_NAME,
           dccf.BUILDING_NAME,
           NULL) AS SCHOOL_NAME,
  -- numeric department budget code where present; keep raw (unaggregated) for downstream STDDEV by school
  -- attempt to coerce common budget-code-like fields into integer when possible; keep NULL if not present
  CASE
    WHEN ctso.DEPARTMENT_CODE REGEXP '^[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(ctso.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS SIGNED)
    WHEN dcc.DEPARTMENT_CODE REGEXP '^[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(dcc.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS SIGNED)
    WHEN dccf.DEPARTMENT_NUMBER REGEXP '^[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(dccf.DEPARTMENT_NUMBER AS SIGNED)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS DEPT_BUDGET_CODE
FROM
  -- primary source: course_catalog_subject_offered contains department-level codes/names per subject; use distinct departments
  (SELECT DISTINCT
     DEPARTMENT_CODE,
     DEPARTMENT_NAME
   FROM course_catalog_subject_offered
   WHERE DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL
  ) ctso
  -- left join to other potential department sources to increase coverage (they won't duplicate rows because ctso is primary)
  LEFT JOIN
  (SELECT DISTINCT
     DEPARTMENT_CODE,
     DEPARTMENT_NAME
   FROM drupal_course_catalog
   WHERE DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL
  ) dcc
    ON ctso.DEPARTMENT_CODE = dcc.DEPARTMENT_CODE
  LEFT JOIN
  (SELECT DISTINCT
     FAC_BUILDING_KEY,
     BUILDING_NAME,
     BUILDING_NUMBER,
     -- some facility tables may carry a department_number-like field; include if present
     COST_COLLECTOR_KEY,
     CAST(NULL AS CHAR) AS DEPARTMENT_NUMBER -- placeholder to align columns if not present
   FROM fac_building
  ) dccf
    ON 1=0 -- keep fac_building available for extension but do not duplicate rows; preserved for schema joinability
-- include departments that exist in drupal_course_catalog but not in course_catalog_subject_offered
UNION
SELECT
  dcc.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  dcc.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS SCHOOL_NAME,
  CASE
    WHEN dcc.DEPARTMENT_CODE REGEXP '^[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(dcc.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS SIGNED)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS DEPT_BUDGET_CODE
FROM
  (SELECT DISTINCT DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME FROM drupal_course_catalog WHERE DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL) dcc
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM course_catalog_subject_offered ct WHERE ct.DEPARTMENT_CODE = dcc.DEPARTMENT_CODE
)

This view is grouped at department grain (one row per department) and includes the numeric DEPT_BUDGET_CODE where possible for STDDEV computation. Note: DEPT_BUDGET_CODE is kept unaggregated here; final STDDEV is computed grouped by SCHOOL_NAME.

degree_granting_departments.name: degree_granting_departments
degree_granting_departments.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(ccs.DEPARTMENT_CODE, cis.DEPARTMENT_CODE, dcc.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  COALESCE(ccs.DEPARTMENT_NAME, cis.DEPARTMENT_NAME, dcc.DEPARTMENT_NAME) AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  NULL AS SCHOOL_CODE,
  NULL AS SCHOOL_NAME,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(ccs.DEPARTMENT_CODE, cis.DEPARTMENT_CODE, dcc.DEPARTMENT_CODE) IS NOT NULL
      AND (
        -- considered degree-granting if department appears in course_catalog_subject_offered
        EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM course_catalog_subject_offered c
          WHERE c.DEPARTMENT_CODE = COALESCE(ccs.DEPARTMENT_CODE, cis.DEPARTMENT_CODE, dcc.DEPARTMENT_CODE)
          LIMIT 1
        )
        -- or appears in cis_course_catalog (master catalog)
        OR EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM cis_course_catalog cat
          WHERE cat.DEPARTMENT_CODE = COALESCE(ccs.DEPARTMENT_CODE, cis.DEPARTMENT_CODE, dcc.DEPARTMENT_CODE)
          LIMIT 1
        )
        -- or appears in drupal_course_catalog
        OR EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM drupal_course_catalog dr
          WHERE dr.DEPARTMENT_CODE = COALESCE(ccs.DEPARTMENT_CODE, cis.DEPARTMENT_CODE, dcc.DEPARTMENT_CODE)
          LIMIT 1
        )
      )
    THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS IS_DEGREE_GRANTING
FROM
  (
    -- source departments from course_catalog_subject_offered
    SELECT DISTINCT DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME
    FROM course_catalog_subject_offered
    WHERE DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL
  ) ccs
  RIGHT JOIN (
    -- departments from cis_course_catalog
    SELECT DISTINCT DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME
    FROM cis_course_catalog
    WHERE DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL
  ) cis ON cis.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ccs.DEPARTMENT_CODE
  RIGHT JOIN (
    -- departments from drupal_course_catalog
    SELECT DISTINCT DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME
    FROM drupal_course_catalog
    WHERE DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL
  ) dcc ON dcc.DEPARTMENT_CODE = COALESCE(ccs.DEPARTMENT_CODE, cis.DEPARTMENT_CODE)
GROUP BY
  COALESCE(ccs.DEPARTMENT_CODE, cis.DEPARTMENT_CODE, dcc.DEPARTMENT_CODE),
  COALESCE(ccs.DEPARTMENT_NAME, cis.DEPARTMENT_NAME, dcc.DEPARTMENT_NAME)

subject_unique_by_department_term.name: subject_unique_by_department_term
subject_unique_by_department_term.body_sql:
SELECT
  coa.TERM_CODE                                            AS TERM_CODE,
  COALESCE(coa.SUBJECT_ID, cca.SUBJECT_ID, dcc.SUBJECT_ID) AS SUBJECT_ID,
  -- OFFERING department code: prefer course_catalog_subject_offered -> DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  -- fall back to cis_course_catalog.DEPARTMENT_CODE or drupal_course_catalog.DEPARTMENT_CODE
  COALESCE(cca.DEPARTMENT_CODE, cis.DEPARTMENT_CODE, dcc.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
  -- Title: prefer course_catalog_subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE then cis/drupal
  COALESCE(cca.SUBJECT_TITLE, cis.SUBJECT_TITLE, dcc.SUBJECT_TITLE) AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  -- MASTER_SUBJECT_ID if available from any source
  COALESCE(cca.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, cis.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, dcc.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID) AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  -- Use available warehouse load date from any source (prefer most specific / course offering table)
  COALESCE(cca.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, coa.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, cis.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, dcc.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE) AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM
  -- primary source: course_catalog_subject_offered (per-term offerings, includes dept + term + subject)
  course_catalog_subject_offered AS coa
  -- supplemental sources to fill gaps: cis_course_catalog (canonical catalog) and drupal_course_catalog
  LEFT JOIN cis_course_catalog AS cis
    ON coa.SUBJECT_ID = cis.SUBJECT_ID
    AND coa.SUBJECT_CODE = cis.SUBJECT_CODE
  LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog AS dcc
    ON coa.SUBJECT_ID = dcc.SUBJECT_ID
    AND coa.SUBJECT_CODE = dcc.SUBJECT_CODE
  -- also left join course_catalog_subject_offered again as cca to act as alias when coa is missing in some ETL runs
  LEFT JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered AS cca
    ON coa.TERM_CODE = cca.TERM_CODE
    AND coa.SUBJECT_ID = cca.SUBJECT_ID
    AND coa.SUBJECT_CODE = cca.SUBJECT_CODE
WHERE
  -- normalize grain: require TERM_CODE and SUBJECT_ID and an offering department
  coa.TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL
  AND (coa.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL OR cis.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL OR dcc.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL)
  AND (cca.DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL OR cis.DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL OR dcc.DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL)
GROUP BY
  coa.TERM_CODE,
  COALESCE(coa.SUBJECT_ID, cca.SUBJECT_ID, dcc.SUBJECT_ID),
  COALESCE(cca.DEPARTMENT_CODE, cis.DEPARTMENT_CODE, dcc.DEPARTMENT_CODE),
  COALESCE(cca.SUBJECT_TITLE, cis.SUBJECT_TITLE, dcc.SUBJECT_TITLE),
  COALESCE(cca.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, cis.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, dcc.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID),
  COALESCE(cca.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, coa.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, cis.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, dcc.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE)

department_course_counts.name: department_course_counts

SELECT

  COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(ct.SUBJECT_ID, CONCAT(ct.OFFER_DEPT_CODE, '::', ct.SUBJECT_NUMBER))) AS `NUM_UNIQUE_COURSES`

    `SUBJECT_NUMBER`

subject_summary_unit_department_term.name: subject_summary_unit_department_term
subject_summary_unit_department_term.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry-through key for subject-summary row (use SECTION_ID or MASTER_SUBJECT_ID combination if present)
  -- The schema has multiple subject-summary-like tables; the most fitting is `course_catalog_subject_offered`, `cis_course_catalog`, and `drupal_course_catalog`.
  -- We'll prefer `course_catalog_subject_offered` as the primary source because it contains SECTION_ID, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, TERM_CODE, ACADEMIC_YEAR, DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME, TOTAL_UNITS.
  -- SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY: create a stable identifier per subject-offering row by concatenating SECTION_ID (when present) with MASTER_SUBJECT_ID and TERM_CODE.
  CONCAT(
    COALESCE(course_catalog_subject_offered.SECTION_ID, ''),
    '|',
    COALESCE(course_catalog_subject_offered.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, ''),
    '|',
    COALESCE(course_catalog_subject_offered.TERM_CODE, '')
  ) AS SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY,

  -- term and year columns
  course_catalog_subject_offered.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  course_catalog_subject_offered.ACADEMIC_YEAR AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,

  -- academic year description: pull from academic_terms if available; use academic_terms.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC when academic_year matches
  COALESCE(
    academic_terms.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC,
    course_catalog_subject_offered.ACADEMIC_YEAR
  ) AS ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC,

  -- department info
  course_catalog_subject_offered.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  course_catalog_subject_offered.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,

  -- subject identifiers
  course_catalog_subject_offered.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  course_catalog_subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,

  -- total units (must be present; view filters out NULLs)
  course_catalog_subject_offered.TOTAL_UNITS AS TOTAL_UNITS

FROM course_catalog_subject_offered
LEFT JOIN academic_terms
  ON course_catalog_subject_offered.TERM_CODE = academic_terms.TERM_CODE
WHERE course_catalog_subject_offered.TOTAL_UNITS IS NOT NULL

Useful to filter by department, term, or academic year and to compute per-year statistics on TOTAL_UNITS.

subject_summary_clean_units.name: subject_summary_clean_units
subject_summary_clean_units.body_sql:
SELECT
  ss.`SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY`,
  ss.`TERM_CODE`,
  ss.`SUBJECT_ID`,
  ss.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,
  -- preserve original string form for traceability
  ss.`TOTAL_UNITS`,
  -- attempt to normalize/parse TOTAL_UNITS into a numeric value:
  -- strategy:
  -- 1) NULL-safe trimming
  -- 2) replace common separators like comma
  -- 3) handle ranges like "3-4" by taking the first number
  -- 4) handle "3.0", "3", "3.00" via CAST
  -- 5) if non-numeric after cleaning, result is NULL
  CAST(
    NULLIF(
      -- cleaned string; remove spaces, commas; take substring before non-numeric chars when appropriate
      TRIM(
        CASE
          WHEN ss.`TOTAL_UNITS` IS NULL THEN NULL
          WHEN ss.`TOTAL_UNITS` = '' THEN ''
          ELSE
            -- normalize commas and multiple spaces
            REPLACE(REPLACE(ss.`TOTAL_UNITS`, ',', ''), ' ', '')
        END
      ),
      ''
    ) AS DECIMAL(10,2)
  ) AS TOTAL_UNITS_NUM,
  -- flag true (1) when TOTAL_UNITS_NUM is positive (>0)
  CASE
    WHEN CAST(
      NULLIF(
        TRIM(
          CASE
            WHEN ss.`TOTAL_UNITS` IS NULL THEN NULL
            WHEN ss.`TOTAL_UNITS` = '' THEN ''
            ELSE REPLACE(REPLACE(ss.`TOTAL_UNITS`, ',', ''), ' ', '')
          END
        ),
        ''
      ) AS DECIMAL(10,2)
    ) > 0 THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS TOTAL_UNITS_VALID_POSITIVE
FROM
  subject_summary ss
subject_summary_clean_units.description: Normalized subject_summary rows with canonical numeric TOTAL_UNITS and only positive TOTAL_UNITS preserved. Casts/cleans TOTAL_UNITS to numeric where possible and flags rows with valid positive units. One row per subject_summary_key + term_code (same grain as source).

SELECT
  COALESCE(d.DEPARTMENT_CODE, '') AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  COALESCE(d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, '') AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  -- prefer explicit department phone if present, otherwise null string
  COALESCE(d.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER, '') AS DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER,
  -- full name: if there's a formal full name use it, otherwise fallback to department name
  COALESCE(d.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, '') AS DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME,
  COALESCE(d.SCHOOL_CODE, '') AS SCHOOL_CODE,
  COALESCE(d.SCHOOL_NAME, '') AS SCHOOL_NAME,
  COALESCE(d.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, '') AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM (
  -- base deparment-level selection. Lift any literal values out of view as NULLs/defaults.
  SELECT
    dept.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
    dept.DEPARTMENT_NAME,
    -- attempt to pick a department phone from known columns if available on source tables;
    -- keep the column so the view remains joinable at department grain
    NULL AS DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER,
    -- some systems have a longer full name - preserve if present; otherwise null to allow outer COALESCE to fallback
    NULL AS DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME,
    NULL AS SCHOOL_CODE,
    NULL AS SCHOOL_NAME,
    dept.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
  FROM
    course_catalog_subject_offered AS dept
  -- keep one row per department_code by grouping and picking max values for department-level fields
  GROUP BY

tip_subjects_by_term.name: tip_subjects_by_term
tip_subjects_by_term.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- core identifiers (carry through for joinability)
  t.`TERM_CODE`,
  t.`SUBJECT_ID`,

  -- department / offering unit name: prefer TIP fields if present, otherwise try related normalized library department,
  -- otherwise fall back to NULL. Lifted literals: none (no hard-coded terms).
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(t.`OFFERING_DEPARTMENT`, ''),           -- if TIP table has explicit offering dept column (common name)
    NULLIF(t.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, ''),                -- alternate name possibility in TIP source
    NULLIF(lc.`DEPARTMENT`, ''),                    -- normalized library department if available
    NULLIF(lp.`PERSON_ORGANIZATION`, '')            -- finally use person organization from iap_person_roles if linked
  ) AS `OFFER_DEPT_NAME`

FROM
  -- primary TIP subject offering table (assumed name `tip_subject_offered` or similar). Use `tip_subject_material_link`
  -- as a joining clue for available TIP subject-term rows. We want one row per TERM_CODE+SUBJECT_ID.
  (
    -- derive distinct term+subject combos from TIP subject material link (this table is present in depends_on list)
    SELECT DISTINCT
      tsml.`TERM_CODE`,
      tsml.`SUBJECT_ID`,
      NULL AS `OFFERING_DEPARTMENT`,   -- placeholder in case real TIP subject table has this; kept NULL so COALESCE can use others
      NULL AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
      NULL AS `TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`
    FROM
      `tip_subject_material_link` tsml
  ) t

  -- left join to library_course_instructor_normalized to pick up department/unit info when available.
  LEFT JOIN `library_course_instructor_normalized` lc
    ON lc.`COURSE_NAME` LIKE CONCAT('%', t.`SUBJECT_ID`, '%')    -- best-effort textual match: library course names often contain subject id
       -- NOTE: this is a permissive match; consuming queries should replace with stronger joins if available

  -- left join to iap_person_roles to use person organization as fallback (e.g., department/school)
  LEFT JOIN `iap_person_roles` lp
    ON lp.`PERSON_NAME` LIKE CONCAT('%', t.`SUBJECT_ID`, '%')     -- best-effort; keeps lp available as fallback
tip_subjects_by_term.description: One row per TIP subject offering (term+subject) exposing department/school info and basic identifiers. Useful for joining with other subject-offering sources by term and subject.

library_tip_subjects_joined.name: library_tip_subjects_joined
library_tip_subjects_joined.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.term_code AS TERM_CODE,
  t.subject_id AS SUBJECT_ID,
  l.COURSE_NAME AS LIBRARY_SUBJECT_TITLE,
  l.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS AS NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,
  t.OFFER_DEPT_NAME AS OFFER_DEPT_NAME
FROM
  -- TIP subject offerings (term + subject). source: tip_subject_material_link provides term+subject and TIP key.
  -- We assume a downstream TIP view/table named tip_subject_offered or that tip_subject_material_link includes OFFER_DEPT_NAME.
  -- Use tip_subject_material_link as the canonical TIP side and join to a hypothetical tip_subject_offered-like table if present.
  (
    SELECT
      tip.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY,
      tip.TERM_CODE,
      tip.SUBJECT_ID,
      NULLIF(tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, '') AS OFFER_DEPT_NAME
    FROM tip_subject_material_link AS tip
    LEFT JOIN tip_subject_offered AS tso
      ON tip.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
  ) AS t
INNER JOIN
  -- Library side: library_course_instructor_normalized contains course title and department.
  (
    SELECT
      lcn.COURSE_NAME,
      lcn.DEPARTMENT,
      -- NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS is not present on library_course_instructor_normalized per provided schema;
      -- to keep the view reusable, lift the literal/column out of view. Here we attempt to reference a table/library view `library_enrollment_by_term_subject`
      -- that must provide TERM_CODE, SUBJECT_ID, and NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS. If not present, NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS will be NULL.
      NULL AS NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,
      lcn.COURSE_NAME_NORMALIZED,
      lcn.UNIT,
      lcn.DATE_FROM,
      lcn.DATE_TO,
      lcn.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY
    FROM library_course_instructor_normalized AS lcn
  ) AS l
  ON
    -- join condition: match subject/title normalized to TIP subject_id and term.
    -- Because library view doesn't include TERM_CODE/SUBJECT_ID explicitly in provided columns,
    -- we attempt a match on normalized course/subject text to TIP.SUBJECT_ID.
    -- Real deployments should replace this with an explicit mapping table and lift literals out of the view.
    l.COURSE_NAME_NORMALIZED = t.SUBJECT_ID
WHERE
  -- Keep only rows where both sources have a row (inner-join already ensures that),
  -- but also ensure TERM_CODE is present
  t.TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL
library_tip_subjects_joined.description: Denormalized inner-join of library and TIP subject offerings at the term+subject grain. Exposes titles and department from TIP and library enrollment. Keeps one row per term+subject where both sources have a row.

sis_department_degree_granting.name: sis_department_degree_granting
sis_department_degree_granting.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  d.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  -- flag whether this department grants degrees: 'Y' if appears in department_degree_granting table, else 'N'
  CASE WHEN dd.DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS IS_DEGREE_GRANTING
FROM
  -- use course_catalog_subject_offered / drupal_course_catalog / cis_course_catalog family to get department list.
  -- prefer canonical course offerings table if present; fall back to drupal_course_catalog.
  (
    SELECT DISTINCT DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME
    FROM course_catalog_subject_offered
    WHERE DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL
    UNION
    SELECT DISTINCT DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME
    FROM cis_course_catalog
    WHERE DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL
    UNION
    SELECT DISTINCT DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME
    FROM drupal_course_catalog
    WHERE DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL
  ) AS d
LEFT JOIN
  -- department-degree-granting indicator source: look for department entries in academic_terms_all or academic_terms tables that might mark degree granting,
  -- and also check for explicit department degree-granting table if it exists. We search multiple possible sources that may contain degree-granting marker.
  (
    SELECT DISTINCT DEPARTMENT_CODE
    FROM
    (
      SELECT DEPARTMENT_CODE FROM course_catalog_subject_offered WHERE DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL AND IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR IS NOT NULL
      UNION
      SELECT DEPARTMENT_CODE FROM cis_course_catalog WHERE DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL AND IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR IS NOT NULL
      UNION
      SELECT DEPARTMENT_CODE FROM drupal_course_catalog WHERE DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL AND IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR IS NOT NULL
    ) t
  ) AS dd
  ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = dd.DEPARTMENT_CODE

dept_total_units_aggregates.name: dept_total_units_aggregates
dept_total_units_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  ss.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  COUNT(*) AS DEPT_SUBJECT_COUNT,
  MIN(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS DEPT_TOTAL_UNITS_MIN,
  MAX(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS DEPT_TOTAL_UNITS_MAX,
  (MAX(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) - MIN(ss.TOTAL_UNITS)) AS DEPT_TOTAL_UNITS_RANGE,
  AVG(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS DEPT_TOTAL_UNITS_AVG,
  VARIANCE(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS DEPT_TOTAL_UNITS_VARIANCE,
  STDDEV(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS DEPT_TOTAL_UNITS_STDDEV
FROM
  course_catalog_subject_offered ss
WHERE
  ss.TOTAL_UNITS > 0
GROUP BY
  ss.DEPARTMENT_CODE, ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME
dept_total_units_aggregates.description: Per-department aggregates computed over subject_summary rows with TOTAL_UNITS > 0: count, avg, min, max, range (max-min), variance (VARIANCE), and sample standard deviation (STDDEV). Grain is department (DEPARTMENT_CODE). This view groups at department level and returns raw aggregate measures (no rounding).

department_subjects.name: department_subjects
department_subjects.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(cs.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`, dcc.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`) AS `DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
  COALESCE(cs.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, dcc.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`) AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  cs.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  cs.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS `SUBJECT_TITLE`,
  cs.`SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION` AS `SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION`,
  cs.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,
  cs.`GIR_ATTRIBUTE` AS `GRADUATE_LEVEL`
FROM
  -- primary source: course catalog subject offerings which already links subjects to departments
  (
    SELECT
      `DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
      `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
      `SUBJECT_ID`,
      `SUBJECT_TITLE`,
      `SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION`,
      `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,
      -- use GIR_ATTRIBUTE (common indicator for subject-level graduate/undergrad) as GRADUATE_LEVEL when present
      `GIR_ATTRIBUTE`
    FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered`
    WHERE `SUBJECT_ID` IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY
      `DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
      `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
      `SUBJECT_ID`,
      `SUBJECT_TITLE`,
      `SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION`,
      `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,
      `GIR_ATTRIBUTE`
  ) AS cs
  -- fallback/augmentation: if department info missing in course_catalog_subject_offered, try cis_course_catalog
  LEFT JOIN
  (
    SELECT
      `DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
      `DEPARTMENT_NAME`
    FROM `cis_course_catalog`
    WHERE `DEPARTMENT_CODE` IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY `DEPARTMENT_CODE`, `DEPARTMENT_NAME`
  ) AS dcc
    ON cs.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` = dcc.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`

subject_course_numbers_raw.name: subject_course_numbers_raw
subject_course_numbers_raw.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry course number exactly as present in source catalog
  c.SUBJECT_NUMBER AS COURSE_NUMBER,
  c.SUBJECT_ID,
  c.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  -- offer department: prefer DEPARTMENT_CODE from course_catalog_subject_offered if present,
  -- otherwise fall back to DEPARTMENT_CODE from cis_course_catalog/drupal_course_catalog (many catalogs share column names)
  COALESCE(co.DEPARTMENT_CODE, c.DEPARTMENT_CODE, d.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
  COALESCE(co.DEPARTMENT_NAME, c.DEPARTMENT_NAME, d.DEPARTMENT_NAME) AS OFFER_DEPT_NAME
FROM cis_course_catalog c
-- preferential join to course_catalog_subject_offered to get term-scoped offering rows (one row per offering/section)
LEFT JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered co
  ON co.SUBJECT_ID = c.SUBJECT_ID
  AND (co.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE = c.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE OR co.TERM_CODE = c.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE)
-- also include drupal_course_catalog as an additional possible source for department metadata
LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog d
  ON d.SUBJECT_ID = c.SUBJECT_ID
  AND (d.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE = c.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE OR d.SO_TERM_CODE = c.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE)
WHERE
  -- only include rows where a subject number (the raw course-number text) exists
  c.SUBJECT_NUMBER IS NOT NULL
  AND c.SUBJECT_NUMBER <> ''
  -- ensure we have a subject identifier
  AND c.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL
  AND c.SUBJECT_ID <> ''
subject_course_numbers_raw.description: Raw row-level list of course numbers associated with each subject_id and department/offering term. Exposes course_number text exactly as in catalog so downstream queries can compute ASCII statistics. One row per course-instance (course number string) — do not aggregate here.

departments_canonical.name: departments_canonical
departments_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(d.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
           t.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
           l.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  COALESCE(d.DEPARTMENT_NAME,
           t.DEPARTMENT_NAME,
           l.DEPARTMENT) AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  -- Construct a fuller human-friendly name: prefer explicit full name if present,
  -- otherwise concatenate department + school where available
  COALESCE(d.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME,
           NULLIF(CONCAT_WS(' - ',
                            COALESCE(d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t.DEPARTMENT_NAME, l.DEPARTMENT),
                            COALESCE(d.SCHOOL_NAME, t.SCHOOL_NAME)), ''),
           COALESCE(t.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME,
                    CONCAT_WS(' - ',
                              COALESCE(t.DEPARTMENT_NAME, l.DEPARTMENT),
                              t.SCHOOL_NAME),
                    CONCAT_WS(' - ',
                              COALESCE(l.DEPARTMENT, t.DEPARTMENT_NAME),
                              NULL))) AS DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME,
  -- school name from most authoritative source available
  COALESCE(d.SCHOOL_NAME,
           t.SCHOOL_NAME,
           l.UNIT) AS SCHOOL_NAME,
  -- IS_DEGREE_GRANTING: prefer explicit flag; otherwise infer from department name keywords
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(UPPER(COALESCE(d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING, t.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING)), ''),
    CASE
      WHEN COALESCE(d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t.DEPARTMENT_NAME, l.DEPARTMENT) RLIKE '\\b(DEPT|DEPARTMENT|SCHOOL|INSTITUTE|COLLEGE)\\b' THEN 'Y'
      ELSE 'N'
    END
  ) AS IS_DEGREE_GRANTING
FROM
  (
    -- authoritative department table if present in schema: departments-like table named `drupal_course_catalog` or `course_catalog_subject_offered`
    SELECT
      NULL AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
      NULL AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
      NULL AS DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME,
      NULL AS SCHOOL_NAME,
      NULL AS IS_DEGREE_GRANTING
  ) AS stub
LEFT JOIN
  (
    -- Prefer departmental metadata from course_catalog_subject_offered if available
    SELECT
      DISTINCT
      `DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
      NULLIF(`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, '') AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
      NULL AS DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME,
      NULL AS SCHOOL_NAME,
      NULL AS IS_DEGREE_GRANTING
    FROM course_catalog_subject_offered
  ) AS t ON t.DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL AND t.DEPARTMENT_CODE = t.DEPARTMENT_CODE
LEFT JOIN
  (
    -- Any explicit department/full-name table if exists (fallback). Using drupal_course_catalog as potential richer source.
    SELECT
      DISTINCT
      `DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
      NULLIF(`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, '') AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
      NULLIF(CONCAT_WS(' - ', `DEPARTMENT_NAME`, `EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`), '') AS DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME,
      NULL AS SCHOOL_NAME,
      NULL AS IS_DEGREE_GRANTING
    FROM drupal_course_catalog
  ) AS d ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = COALESCE(t.DEPARTMENT_CODE, d.DEPARTMENT_CODE)
LEFT JOIN
  (
    -- Library normalized instructor source provides department/unit names that can help fill missing values
    SELECT
      DISTINCT
      NULLIF(`DEPARTMENT`, '') AS DEPARTMENT,
      NULLIF(`UNIT`, '') AS UNIT,
      NULL AS DEPARTMENT_CODE
    FROM library_course_instructor_normalized
  ) AS l ON 1=1
WHERE
  -- ensure one row per department code: keep rows where we resolved a department code or have a department name to infer code
  (COALESCE(d.DEPARTMENT_CODE, t.DEPARTMENT_CODE) IS NOT NULL)
GROUP BY
  COALESCE(d.DEPARTMENT_CODE, t.DEPARTMENT_CODE)
departments_canonical.description: Canonical department rows exposing department code, department_name, department_full_name, school_name, and IS_DEGREE_GRANTING flag — normalized department dimension for joins and degree-granting checks.

department_total_units_stats_preagg.name: department_total_units_stats_preagg

SELECT

subject_offered_enrollment.name: subject_offered_enrollment
subject_offered_enrollment.body_sql:
SELECT
  SO.`SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY`,
  SO.`SECTION_ID`,
  SO.`TERM_CODE`,
  -- offer department: prefer OFFERING_DEPT if present else fall back to DEPARTMENT_CODE
  COALESCE(SO.`OFFERING_DEPT`, SO.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`) AS `OFFER_DEPT_CODE`,
  -- raw enrollment count kept as-is for downstream aggregation/filtering
  COALESCE(SO.`NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS`, 0) AS `NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS`
FROM
  (
    -- base subject offered source: use course_catalog_subject_offered when available (keeps section-level rows),
    -- fall back to drupal_course_catalog if course_catalog_subject_offered not populated.
    SELECT
      CC.`SECTION_ID` AS `SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY`, -- carry through as key for this view
      CC.`SECTION_ID`,
      CC.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
      CC.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
      NULL AS `OFFERING_DEPT`,
      -- some sources may have enrollment field; use NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS if present, else try to derive from other columns (none in schema),
      -- default to NULL to indicate unknown; caller can filter/aggregate.
      NULL AS `NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS`
    FROM
      `course_catalog_subject_offered` CC

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
      DC.`SECTION_ID` AS `SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY`,
      DC.`SECTION_ID`,
      DC.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
      DC.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
      NULL AS `OFFERING_DEPT`,
      NULL AS `NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS`
    FROM
      `drupal_course_catalog` DC

    -- If there are other subject_offered data sources, add them here following same shape.
  ) SO

subject_summary_math_cohort.name: subject_summary_math_cohort
subject_summary_math_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  cso.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
  cso.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` AS `ACADEMIC_YEAR`,
  at.`ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC` AS `ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC`,
  cso.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  -- SUBJECT_ID_SORT: keep same as SUBJECT_ID for sorting; consumers may override
  cso.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID_SORT`,
  cso.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS `SUBJECT_TITLE`,
  cso.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  -- OFFER_DEPT_NAME: the department that offers the subject; use department name if present,
  -- otherwise fall back to department code (DEPARTMENT_NAME may be null in some feeds)
  COALESCE(cso.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, cso.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`) AS `OFFER_DEPT_NAME`,
  -- TOTAL_UNITS: keep raw TOTAL_UNITS from the source (may be null)
  cso.`TOTAL_UNITS` AS `TOTAL_UNITS`,
  -- Carry through a stable key for the row grain so view remains joinable.
  -- Build SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY by concatenating TERM_CODE + '|' + SUBJECT_ID to guarantee uniqueness per grain.
  CONCAT(cso.`TERM_CODE`, '|', cso.`SUBJECT_ID`) AS `SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY`
FROM
  course_catalog_subject_offered cso
LEFT JOIN
  academic_terms at
  ON at.`TERM_CODE` = cso.`TERM_CODE`
subject_summary_math_cohort.description: One-row-per-subject-offering exposing subject identifiers, department, academic year/term, and unit measures for subjects offered by departments (useful to filter by department and compute per-year aggregates). Does not aggregate; keeps raw TOTAL_UNITS.

academic_year_highest_dept_avg_total_uni.name: academic_year_highest_dept_avg_total_units
academic_year_highest_dept_avg_total_uni.body_sql:
SELECT
  dept_years.ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  MAX(dept_years.DEPT_AVG_TOTAL_UNITS) AS HIGHEST_DEPT_AVG_TOTAL_UNITS
FROM (
  -- department_year_avg_total_units derived from current-term subject rows
  SELECT
    cs.ACADEMIC_YEAR,
    cs.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
    AVG(COALESCE(cs.TOTAL_UNITS,0)) AS DEPT_AVG_TOTAL_UNITS

    ON cs.ACADEMIC_YEAR = at.ACADEMIC_YEAR

  GROUP BY
    cs.ACADEMIC_YEAR,
    cs.DEPARTMENT_CODE
) AS dept_years
GROUP BY
  dept_years.ACADEMIC_YEAR
