sis_department_degree_granting_74.name: sis_department_degree_granting_74
sis_department_degree_granting_74.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  d.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  -- Prefer a full/display name if available; otherwise use the short name
  COALESCE(d.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, d.DEPARTMENT_NAME) AS DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME,
  -- Canonicalized flag (degree-granting). Lift literal: treat 'Y' as degree-granting in calling queries if needed.
  d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING AS IS_DEGREE_GRANTING
FROM (
  SELECT
    -- carry through the department code as the key/grain
    department_code AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
    -- display name columns commonly present in SIS department sources
    department_name AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
    department_full_name AS DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME,
    -- canonicalized flag column (text); keep as-is so callers can interpret values ('Y'/'N', '1'/'0', etc.)
    is_degree_granting AS IS_DEGREE_GRANTING,
    -- row-number in case there are duplicates per DEPARTMENT_CODE; prefer rows where is_degree_granting indicates true,
    -- then the most recently loaded row if such metadata exists. We keep deterministic ordering using COALESCE on warehouse load date where available.
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY department_code
      ORDER BY
        -- prefer explicit degree-granting markers first (non-null sort high). This ORDER BY uses a boolean expression to prioritize likely degree-granting rows.
        (CASE
           WHEN is_degree_granting IN ('Y','y','1','true','T') THEN 1
           ELSE 0
         END) DESC,
        -- next prefer rows with a warehouse load date (most recent). If column absent, NULLs sort last.
        COALESCE(STR_TO_DATE(warehouse_load_date, '%Y-%m-%d'), STR_TO_DATE(warehouse_load_date, '%Y/%m/%d')) DESC,
        -- finally deterministic fallback
        department_name
    ) AS rn
  FROM
    -- source SIS department table(s). Lift actual table name out of view; callers can replace with real SIS table if needed.
    -- For portability we select from `academic_terms` as a placeholder source that exists in the schema, but the view expects a SIS departments-like table named `sis_departments`.
    -- Replace `sis_departments` with the real table when deploying.
    (SELECT
       NULL AS department_code,
       NULL AS department_name,
       NULL AS department_full_name,
       NULL AS is_degree_granting,
       NULL AS warehouse_load_date
    ) AS sis_departments_placeholder
) d
WHERE d.rn = 1
source_tables: sis_departments (expected real SIS table; placeholder used in view body)
sis_department_degree_granting_74.description: One-row-per-department from SIS department filtered to departments that are degree-granting (canonicalized flag). Keeps identifying and display name columns needed to join to admin dept and course/cip data.

department_course_cip_codes.name: department_course_cip_codes
department_course_cip_codes.body_sql:
SELECT
  soa.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  soa.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  soa.SUBJECT_NUMBER AS COURSE_NUMBER,
  soa.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  soa.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
  cip.PROGRAM_CODE AS CIP_PROGRAM_CODE
FROM
  course_catalog_subject_offered AS soa
LEFT JOIN
  cis_course_catalog AS cis
    ON cis.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = soa.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
    AND cis.SUBJECT_CODE = soa.SUBJECT_CODE
    -- lift any term literal out of the view; keep join permissive across terms
LEFT JOIN
  cip AS cip
    ON (
      -- try to join CIP by matching department/program relationships:
      -- prefer matching by FOUR_DIGIT_CODE if subject number looks like a 4-digit CIP,
      -- otherwise match by PROGRAM_TITLE / SUBJECT_TITLE fuzzy equality (best-effort exact)
      cip.PROGRAM_CODE = soa.DEPARTMENT_CODE
      OR cip.PROGRAM_CODE = cis.DEPARTMENT_CODE
      OR cip.PROGRAM_TITLE = cis.SUBJECT_TITLE
      OR cip.FOUR_DIGIT_CODE = SUBSTRING(soa.SUBJECT_NUMBER, 1, 4)
    )
department_course_cip_codes.description: One row per course (subject) offering linking the offering's department to the CIP program code(s) associated with that course where available. Exposes course identifiers and the CIP PROGRAM_CODE so numeric comparisons can be applied later. Does not aggregate — leaves one row per subject/course instance.

fac_building_core.name: fac_building_core
fac_building_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.`FAC_BUILDING_KEY` AS `FAC_BUILDING_KEY`,
  -- carry a BUILDING_KEY column through for joins/use; prefer BUILDING_NUMBER if available
  NULL AS `BUILDING_KEY`,
  f.`BUILDING_NUMBER` AS `BUILDING_NUMBER`,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(f.`BUILDING_NAME`, ''), f.`BUILDING_NAME`) AS `BUILDING_NAME`,
  f.`BUILDING_TYPE` AS `BUILDING_TYPE`,
  f.`SITE` AS `SITE`,
  f.`ASSIGNABLE_AREA` AS `ASSIGNABLE_AREA`,
  f.`EXT_GROSS_AREA` AS `EXT_GROSS_AREA`,
  f.`NUM_OF_ROOMS` AS `NUM_OF_ROOMS`
FROM `fac_building` f
fac_building_core.description: One row per building (fac_building). Canonical projection of building identifiers and key numeric attributes used in analysis (ASSIGNABLE_AREA, EXT_GROSS_AREA) plus BUILDING_TYPE and SITE for filtering/grouping.

building_room_join.name: building_room_join
building_room_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY,
  fr.BUILDING_KEY AS `fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY`,
  fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY AS `fac_building.FAC_BUILDING_KEY`,
  fb.BUILDING_TYPE AS `fac_building.BUILDING_TYPE`,
  fb.SITE AS `fac_building.SITE`,
  fb.ASSIGNABLE_AREA AS `fac_building.ASSIGNABLE_AREA`,
  fr.AREA AS `fac_rooms.AREA`
FROM fac_rooms fr
JOIN fac_building fb
  ON fr.BUILDING_KEY = fb.BUILDING_NUMBER
WHERE COALESCE(fr.AREA,0) > 0
building_room_join.description: Denormalized row-level view that joins fac_building (building attributes) to fac_rooms (room-level rows restricted to AREA > 0). One row per room-with-positive-area enriched with its building-level attributes. Useful for grouping by building type/site and computing room-level aggregates (including geometric mean) while also allowing building-level aggregates (assignable area) and filtering to buildings that have qualifying rooms.

sis_course_description_filtered.name: sis_course_description_filtered
sis_course_description_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical course identifier that will be used to join (carry through)
  `COURSE`,

  -- department code and name
  `DEPARTMENT`,
  `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,

  -- short and long descriptions (canonical)
  `COURSE_DESCRIPTION`,
  `COURSE_DESCRIPTION_LONG`,

  -- degree-granting indicator exposed as a normalized flag ('Y'/'N'/NULL preserved)
  `IS_DEGREE_GRANTING`,

  `FROM_TERM`,

FROM
  sis_course_description
sis_course_description_filtered.description: One row per course (course identifier) from sis_course_description with canonical course description fields and degree-granting flag exposed. This isolates course descriptive text and degree-granting indicator for joining to subject lists.

subject_offered_engineering_cohort.name: subject_offered_engineering_cohort
subject_offered_engineering_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- primary key carried through
  CAST(coso.SECTION_ID AS CHAR) AS SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY,

  -- subject key (keep raw)
  CAST(coso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID AS CHAR) AS SUBJECT_KEY,

  -- term and subject identifiers
  CAST(coso.TERM_CODE AS CHAR) AS TERM_CODE,
  CAST(coso.SUBJECT_ID AS CHAR) AS SUBJECT_ID,

  -- offering department raw columns (kept for later aggregation)
  CAST(coso.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS CHAR) AS OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
  CAST(coso.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS CHAR) AS OFFER_DEPT_NAME,

  -- derive school name from department_code using simple mapping;
  -- lift specific school literal(s) out of the view (use SCHOOL_NAME parameter when selecting from this view)
  -- For portability keep SCHOOL_NAME as the department's high-level school label when available,
  -- otherwise NULL. Consumers should filter SCHOOL_NAME = <school_literal>.
  CASE
    WHEN coso.DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN LEFT(coso.DEPARTMENT_CODE,3) IN ('16-', '16_') THEN 'School of Engineering'
    WHEN LEFT(coso.DEPARTMENT_CODE,2) IN ('16') THEN 'School of Engineering'
    ELSE coso.HGN_DESC
  END AS SCHOOL_NAME,

  -- raw enrollment kept for later aggregation; many catalogs store enrollment in MEET_TIME / custom columns.
  -- If NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS exists use it; otherwise NULL. Keep as integer when possible.
  -- Many source tables don't have this column — preserve by selecting possible known field names if present.
  NULL AS NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,

  -- warehouse load tracking
  CAST(coso.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE AS CHAR) AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE

FROM course_catalog_subject_offered AS coso

-- Row-level cohort restrictions:
-- 1) require non-null SUBJECT_ID
-- 2) restrict to records that belong to the School of Engineering (consumers to provide exact literal)
-- 3) exclude specified departments (lifted out: consumers should filter with OFFER_DEPT_CODE NOT IN (...))
WHERE coso.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL
  AND (
    -- basic heuristic for School of Engineering based on department codes/patterns.
    -- Consumers should filter by SCHOOL_NAME = 'School of Engineering' when selecting from view.
    LEFT(coso.DEPARTMENT_CODE,2) = '16'
    OR LEFT(coso.DEPARTMENT_CODE,3) IN ('16-','16_')
    OR coso.DEPARTMENT_NAME LIKE '%Engineering%'
  )
subject_offered_engineering_cohort.description: Row-level cohort of subject_offered rows restricted to records with a non-null SUBJECT_ID and belonging to a specified school (e.g. School of Engineering) and excluding specified departments. Keep raw enrollment and dept columns for later aggregation.

master_dept_hierarchy_dlc.name: master_dept_hierarchy_dlc
master_dept_hierarchy_dlc.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.`DLC_KEY` AS `DLC_KEY`,
  d.`DLC_NAME` AS `DLC_NAME`,
  NULL AS `DLC_CODE`,
  -- Normalize MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_1_CODE and NAME from DLC_NAME for case-insensitive filters/joins.
  -- We preserve original casing in NAME, and provide an uppercase code for joins.
  UPPER(TRIM(d.`DLC_NAME`)) AS `MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_1_CODE`,
  TRIM(d.`DLC_NAME`) AS `MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_1_NAME`,
  -- Attempt to pull a warehouse load date if present on DLC core; otherwise NULL.
  NULL AS `WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE`
FROM
  -- base DLC lookup rows
  dlc_core d

semantic_filters.none: no intrinsic filters; keep all DLC rows

master_dept_hierarchy_dlc.description: DLC lookup rows: one row per DLC key with its DLC_NAME and hierarchy attributes for case-insensitive name filters and joins to facility organizations.

math_subjects_by_academic_year_aggregate.name: math_subjects_by_academic_year_aggregates
math_subjects_by_academic_year_aggregate.body_sql:
SELECT
  ss.ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  MAX(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS MAX_TOTAL_UNITS,
  MIN(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS MIN_TOTAL_UNITS,
  (MAX(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) - MIN(ss.TOTAL_UNITS)) AS TOTAL_UNITS_RANGE,
  VARIANCE(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS TOTAL_UNITS_VARIANCE,
  COUNT(*) AS NUM_SUBJECTS
FROM cis_course_catalog AS ss
WHERE ss.SUBJECT_CODE = 'MAT' -- lift subject literal out if needed; currently filters to Mathematics
  AND ss.ACADEMIC_YEAR IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ss.ACADEMIC_YEAR
math_subjects_by_academic_year_aggregate.description: Aggregated measures for Mathematics subjects grouped by academic year: computes count, max_total_units, min_total_units, range (max-min), and population variance of TOTAL_UNITS across all Mathematics subject_summary rows in that academic year. One row per academic year.

subject_summary_with_term_and_dept.name: subject_summary_with_term_and_dept
subject_summary_with_term_and_dept.body_sql:
SELECT
  ss.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY,
  at.TERM_CODE,
  at.TERM_START_DATE,
  at.IS_REGULAR_TERM,
  at.TERM_STATUS_INDICATOR,
  at.ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  ss.SUBJECT_ID,
  ss.SUBJECT_TITLE,
  ss.TOTAL_UNITS
FROM subject_summary AS ss
LEFT JOIN academic_terms AS at
  ON ss.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE
  -- carry through term key if needed (not requested in output)

semantic_filters.TOTAL_UNITS: EXPOSED (no further filter) -- keep NULLs if caller wants them; question-specific filters applied externally

subject_summary_with_term_and_dept.description: Denormalized subject_summary rows joined to academic_terms to expose TERM_START_DATE, IS_REGULAR_TERM / TERM_STATUS_INDICATOR and ACADEMIC_YEAR from term table, and department name from subject_summary. This is a general-purpose joined relation of subject summaries with term metadata for filtering by term dates and regular-term flags.

subject_summary_per_department_term.name: subject_summary_per_department_term
subject_summary_per_department_term.body_sql:
SELECT
  `TERM_CODE`,
  `SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY`,
  `SUBJECT_ID`,
  `SUBJECT_TITLE`,
  -- keep raw value but ensure it's numeric-castable: return original string when cast succeeds, else NULL
  CASE
    WHEN `SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER` REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$' THEN `SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER`
    ELSE NULL
  END AS `SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER`,
  `DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
  `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  `SCHOOL_CODE`,
  `SCHOOL_NAME`
FROM
  subject_summary
WHERE
  `SUBJECT_TITLE` IS NOT NULL
  AND `SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY` IS NOT NULL
  -- ensure enrollment is present and castable numeric; keep rows with NULL enrollment only if original value is NULL but spec says ensures castable numeric (keeps raw value)
  AND (
    `SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER` IS NULL
    OR `SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER` REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$'
  )
subject_summary_per_department_term.description: Normalized rows of subject summary offerings exposing subject title, enrollment and department/school keys. One row per subject offering as recorded in subject_summary (term x subject). Filters and cleaning: excludes NULL SUBJECT_TITLE and ensures SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER is castable numeric (keeps raw value).

degree_granting_departments_84.name: degree_granting_departments_84
degree_granting_departments_84.body_sql:
SELECT
  `DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
  `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  `SCHOOL_CODE`,
  `SCHOOL_NAME`,
  `IS_DEGREE_GRANTING`
FROM
  sis_department
WHERE
  -- keep only departments marked as degree-granting; literal values (e.g. 'Y') should be provided by callers if needed
  `IS_DEGREE_GRANTING` IS NOT NULL

semantic_filters.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING: IS NOT NULL AND IS_DEGREE_GRANTING != '0' AND IS_DEGREE_GRANTING != ''

degree_granting_departments_84.description: Cohort of departments that are degree-granting according to sis_department.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING. Exposes department and school identifiers and names for joins and grouping. Does not apply question-specific exclusions like 'Political Science'.

department_subject_metrics.name: department_subject_metrics
department_subject_metrics.body_sql:
SELECT
  ss.SCHOOL_CODE,
  ss.SCHOOL_NAME,
  ss.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  ss.SUBJECT_TITLE,
  SUM(IFNULL(ss.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER,0)) AS SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_SUM
FROM
  subject_summary ss
GROUP BY
  ss.SCHOOL_CODE,
  ss.SCHOOL_NAME,
  ss.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  ss.SUBJECT_TITLE
department_subject_metrics.description: Aggregated subject-level metrics per department and school: for each department (per SCHOOL_CODE, DEPARTMENT_CODE) compute distinct SUBJECT_TITLE count and sum of SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER, but keep the row-level subjects' identity to allow deduping across departments when building school totals. This view groups at department x subject_title level producing one row per unique subject title within the department with its total enrollment (sum across terms/sections as recorded in subject_summary).

degree_granting_departments_cohort_86.name: degree_granting_departments_cohort_86

  `IS_DEGREE_GRANTING`,

degree_granting_departments_cohort_86.description: One row per department from sis_department that is marked as degree-granting (truthy IS_DEGREE_GRANTING). Exposes department identifiers and textual name for downstream joins/filters.

iap_activity_rows.name: iap_activity_rows
iap_activity_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- keys carried through so the view is joinable at the required grain
  `IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY`,
  `IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`,
  `IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY`,
  `TERM_CODE`,

  -- descriptive/activity metadata
  `ACTIVITY_TITLE`,

  -- enrollment / capacity metrics
  CAST(NULLIF(`MAX_ENROLLMENT`, '') AS SIGNED) AS `MAX_ENROLLMENT`,
  CAST(NULLIF(`ATTENDANCE`, '') AS SIGNED) AS `ATTENDANCE`,

  -- status / last updated
  CASE
    WHEN `IS_CANCELLED` IS NULL OR `IS_CANCELLED` = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN UPPER(`IS_CANCELLED`) IN ('Y','YES','1','TRUE') THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS `IS_CANCELLED`,
  `LAST_ACTIVITY_DATE`
FROM
  `iap_subject_detail`
iap_activity_rows.description: One row per IAP activity offering (iap_subject_detail). Exposes activity identifiers, term code, enrollment and metadata useful to filter/rank IAP activities.

catalog_subject_course.name: catalog_subject_course
catalog_subject_course.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,
  c.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  c.`SUBJECT_CODE` AS `SUBJECT_CODE`,
  c.`SUBJECT_NUMBER` AS `SUBJECT_NUMBER`,
  c.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS `SUBJECT_TITLE`,
  c.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS `DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
  c.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  c.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` AS `EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`,
  c.`LECTURE_UNITS` AS `LECTURE_UNITS`,
  c.`TOTAL_UNITS` AS `TOTAL_UNITS`,
  c.`HGN_CODE` AS `HGN_CODE`
FROM `cis_course_catalog` c
-- The view's grain is one row per SUBJECT_ID and EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE.
-- Preserve subject identifiers and term so rows remain joinable to term-specific data.
GROUP BY
  c.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,
  c.`SUBJECT_ID`,
  c.`SUBJECT_CODE`,
  c.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`,
  c.`SUBJECT_TITLE`,
  c.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
  c.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  c.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`,
  c.`LECTURE_UNITS`,
  c.`TOTAL_UNITS`,
  c.`HGN_CODE`
catalog_subject_course.description: Catalog/course subject rows (from cis_course_catalog and related subject summary tables) exposing subject identifiers, department offering, subject title, and lecture units. One row per catalog subject (subject-course combination) keyed by SUBJECT_ID (and EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE where present) to allow linking to term-specific catalog data.

subject_summary_rows.name: subject_summary_rows
subject_summary_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- key: compose a stable SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY from TERM_CODE and SUBJECT_ID
  CONCAT(COALESCE(ctso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE, ctso.TERM_CODE, ''), '||', COALESCE(ctso.SUBJECT_ID, '')) AS SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY,
  -- term and subject identifiers (carry-through for joinability)
  COALESCE(ctso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE, ctso.TERM_CODE) AS TERM_CODE,
  ctso.SUBJECT_ID,
  -- descriptive fields
  COALESCE(ctso.SUBJECT_TITLE, ccc.SUBJECT_TITLE, dcc.SUBJECT_TITLE) AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  COALESCE(ctso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, ccc.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, dcc.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID) AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  COALESCE(ctso.DEPARTMENT_CODE, ccc.DEPARTMENT_CODE, dcc.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  COALESCE(ctso.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ccc.DEPARTMENT_NAME, dcc.DEPARTMENT_NAME) AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  -- derive school code/name from department when available; lift literals out of view: callers provide mapping if needed.
  NULL AS SCHOOL_CODE,
  NULL AS SCHOOL_NAME,
  -- measures: canonical TOTAL_UNITS from available subject-offered / catalog tables
  COALESCE(ctso.TOTAL_UNITS, ccc.TOTAL_UNITS, dcc.TOTAL_UNITS) AS TOTAL_UNITS,
  -- warehouse load date: pick most specific available
  COALESCE(ctso.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, ccc.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, dcc.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE) AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM
  -- course_catalog_subject_offered is the primary canonical cohort of subject offerings per term
  course_catalog_subject_offered ctso
  -- left join other catalogs as fallbacks for metadata
  LEFT JOIN cis_course_catalog ccc
    ON ctso.SUBJECT_ID = ccc.SUBJECT_ID
    AND COALESCE(ctso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE, ctso.TERM_CODE) = ccc.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE
  LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog dcc
    ON ctso.SUBJECT_ID = dcc.SUBJECT_ID
    AND COALESCE(ctso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE, ctso.TERM_CODE) = dcc.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE
subject_summary_rows.description: One row per subject summary offering (term + subject) with key descriptive and measure columns. Use this as the canonical cohort of subjects with TOTAL_UNITS and department/school metadata.

subject_offered_fall_nonvariable_cohort.name: subject_offered_fall_nonvariable_cohort
subject_offered_fall_nonvariable_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT_WS('|', COALESCE(cos.`SECTION_ID`, ''), COALESCE(cos.`TERM_CODE`, ''), COALESCE(cos.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`, '')) AS `SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY`,
  COALESCE(cos.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`, '') AS `SUBJECT_KEY`,
  cos.`SECTION_ID`,
  cos.`TERM_CODE`,
  cos.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,
  cos.`SUBJECT_ID`,
  cos.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS `OFFER_DEPT_CODE`,
  cos.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `OFFER_DEPT_NAME`,
  cos.`IS_VARIABLE_UNITS`,
  cos.`IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM`,
  cos.`WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE`
FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered` AS cos
WHERE
  -- restrict to fall term offerings
  COALESCE(cos.`IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM`, '') <> ''
  AND (UPPER(COALESCE(cos.`IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM`, '')) = 'Y' OR UPPER(COALESCE(cos.`IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM`, '')) = 'TRUE' OR UPPER(COALESCE(cos.`IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM`, '')) = 'T' OR UPPER(COALESCE(cos.`IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM`, '')) = '1')
  -- restrict to non-variable-units subjects
  AND (COALESCE(cos.`IS_VARIABLE_UNITS`, '') = '' OR UPPER(COALESCE(cos.`IS_VARIABLE_UNITS`, '')) IN ('N','FALSE','F','0'))
subject_offered_fall_nonvariable_cohort.description: One-row-per subject offering (section-level) restricted to fall-term offerings and non-variable-units subjects. Exposes identifiers and academic term/year and department info for counting distinct subjects per department and year.

subject_summary_by_term_department.name: subject_summary_by_term_department
subject_summary_by_term_department.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- primary key for the subject_summary row (carry through if exists)
  COALESCE(cso.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY, CONCAT(cso.SUBJECT_ID, '_', at.TERM_CODE)) AS SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY,
  at.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  cso.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  cso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  COALESCE(cso.SUBJECT_TITLE, cso.SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE) AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  COALESCE(cso.DEPARTMENT_CODE, cso.DEPARTMENT) AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  at.ACADEMIC_YEAR AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  cso.TOTAL_UNITS AS TOTAL_UNITS,
  -- canonicalize offered-in-fall flag to 'Y'/'N'/'UNKNOWN' (lift literal decisions out of view; here preserve source)
  cso.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM AS IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM,
  cso.IS_VARIABLE_UNITS AS IS_VARIABLE_UNITS,
  -- prefer a term-level load date when available, fall back to subject row
  COALESCE(at.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, cso.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE) AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM
  -- source: canonical subject summary / course catalog-like table(s)
  -- try common table names in schema: course_catalog_subject_offered, cis_course_catalog, drupal_course_catalog
  (
    SELECT
      SUBJECT_ID,
      MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
      SUBJECT_TITLE,
      SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE,
      DEPARTMENT_CODE,
      DEPARTMENT_NAME,
      TOTAL_UNITS,
      IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM,
      IS_VARIABLE_UNITS,
      WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,
      -- if there is a stable key use it; many source tables don't have SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY so leave NULL
      NULL AS SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY,
      NULL AS DEPARTMENT
    FROM course_catalog_subject_offered

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
      SUBJECT_ID,
      MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
      SUBJECT_TITLE,
      SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE,
      DEPARTMENT_CODE,
      DEPARTMENT_NAME,
      TOTAL_UNITS,
      IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM,
      IS_VARIABLE_UNITS,
      WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,
      NULL AS SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY,
      NULL AS DEPARTMENT
    FROM cis_course_catalog

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
      SUBJECT_ID,
      MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
      SUBJECT_TITLE,
      SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE,
      DEPARTMENT_CODE,
      DEPARTMENT_NAME,
      TOTAL_UNITS,
      IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM,
      IS_VARIABLE_UNITS,
      WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,
      NULL AS SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY,
      NULL AS DEPARTMENT
    FROM drupal_course_catalog
  ) AS cso
JOIN
  -- term metadata to bring TERM_CODE and ACADEMIC_YEAR; academic_terms and academic_terms_all are available
  (
    SELECT
      TERM_CODE,
      ACADEMIC_YEAR,
      WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
    FROM academic_terms

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
      TERM_CODE,
      ACADEMIC_YEAR,
      WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
    FROM academic_terms_all
  ) AS at
  -- join strategy: this view's grain is one row per SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY + TERM_CODE.
  -- we don't have a direct mapping table in schema; to remain generic, cross join subjects to terms so callers can filter by TERM_CODE.
  ON 1 = 1
WHERE
  -- liftable predicates (none) but ensure required columns not null at grain level
  cso.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL
subject_summary_by_term_department.description: Canonicalized subject summary rows with term, academic year and department-level attributes. One row per subject_summary key + TERM_CODE. Useful to count subjects per department per academic year and to join to term metadata.

department_subject_counts_per_academic_y.name: department_subject_counts_per_academic_year
department_subject_counts_per_academic_y.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  c.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  c.DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.SUBJECT_ID) AS DEPARTMENT_SUBJECT_COUNT
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered c
-- only include fall offerings and non-variable unit subjects:
WHERE c.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM = 'Y'
  AND (c.IS_VARIABLE_UNITS IS NULL OR c.IS_VARIABLE_UNITS = 'N')
  -- department code should be present; liftable literal so kept generic (no hard-coded filtering)
GROUP BY
  c.ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  c.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  c.DEPARTMENT_NAME
department_subject_counts_per_academic_y.description: Pre-aggregated counts of distinct subjects offered in fall (non-variable) per department per academic year. One row per (ACADEMIC_YEAR, DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME) with raw count measure. Designed for computing per-year variance, stddev and max across departments.

subject_records_with_term_and_dept.name: subject_records_with_term_and_dept
subject_records_with_term_and_dept.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- key: one row per subject offering (use SECTION_ID from source tables as the offered-summary key where available;
  -- fall back to concatenation of TERM_CODE and SUBJECT_ID if SECTION_ID is not present)
  COALESCE(course_catalog_subject_offered.SECTION_ID,
           CONCAT(course_catalog_subject_offered.TERM_CODE, '::', course_catalog_subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID)) AS SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY,

  -- subject-level key (master subject id when present, otherwise SUBJECT_ID)
  COALESCE(course_catalog_subject_offered.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
           course_catalog_subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID) AS SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY,

  -- term linking key (exposed so downstream filters can be applied)
  course_catalog_subject_offered.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,

  -- requested measure from the offering record
  course_catalog_subject_offered.TOTAL_UNITS AS TOTAL_UNITS,

  -- term duration attribute from the offering row
  course_catalog_subject_offered.TERM_DURATION AS TERM_DURATION,

  -- the offering department name when present (some sources include OFFER_DEPT_NAME; prefer that if available)
  COALESCE(course_catalog_subject_offered.DEPARTMENT_NAME,
           course_catalog_subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
           '') AS OFFER_DEPT_NAME,

  -- canonical department name column (if different; here we expose DEPARTMENT_NAME as available)
  course_catalog_subject_offered.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,

  -- master subject id passed through for joinability
  course_catalog_subject_offered.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,

  -- subject identifier
  course_catalog_subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID

FROM course_catalog_subject_offered
subject_records_with_term_and_dept.description: One-row-per-subject-offering enriched with its term attributes and department/offer-department fields. Exposes TOTAL_UNITS, TERM_CODE, TERM_DURATION, OFFER_DEPT_NAME/DEPARTMENT_NAME (where available) and the academic term linking keys so downstream filters (current term, term status, academic year) can be applied.

subjects_with_academic_year.name: subjects_with_academic_year
subjects_with_academic_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(cos.`SECTION_ID` AS CHAR) AS `SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY`,
  CAST(cos.`TERM_CODE` AS CHAR) AS `TERM_CODE`,
  CAST(at.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` AS CHAR) AS `ACADEMIC_YEAR`,
  CAST(at.`ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC` AS CHAR) AS `ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC`,
  cos.`TOTAL_UNITS` AS `TOTAL_UNITS`,
  -- OFFER_DEPT_NAME: prefer the department name on the course_offering row if present, else fall back to department_name from catalog/drupal
  COALESCE(NULLIF(cos.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, ''), NULLIF(drc.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, ''), NULLIF(ccs.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, '')) AS `OFFER_DEPT_NAME`,
  -- DEPARTMENT_NAME: canonical department name (if multiple sources exist prefer course_catalog_subject_offered then drupal_course_catalog then cis_course_catalog)
  COALESCE(NULLIF(ccs.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, ''), NULLIF(drc.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, ''), NULLIF(cis.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, '')) AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  -- TERM_DURATION: pull from the most specific source available on offering, then catalog tables
  COALESCE(NULLIF(cos.`TERM_DURATION`, ''), NULLIF(ccs.`TERM_DURATION`, ''), NULLIF(drc.`TERM_DURATION`, ''), NULLIF(cis.`TERM_DURATION`, '')) AS `TERM_DURATION`
FROM
  -- primary grain: one row per subject offering summary (use course_catalog_subject_offered as the authoritative subject-offered rows)
  `course_catalog_subject_offered` cos
  -- join to canonical academic_terms mapping by TERM_CODE to get academic year and description
  LEFT JOIN `academic_terms` at
    ON cos.`TERM_CODE` = at.`TERM_CODE`
  -- also left join the all-terms table in case canonical term not present (helps attach academic year)
  LEFT JOIN `academic_terms_all` ata
    ON at.`TERM_CODE` IS NULL AND cos.`TERM_CODE` = ata.`TERM_CODE`
  -- prefer academic_terms but fall back to academic_terms_all via COALESCE above; to ensure fields available, coerce via SELECT expressions
  -- join to drupal_course_catalog (may provide department names / term_duration)
  LEFT JOIN `drupal_course_catalog` drc
    ON cos.`SECTION_ID` = drc.`SECTION_ID` AND cos.`TERM_CODE` = drc.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`
  -- join to cis_course_catalog as another source for department names / term_duration
  LEFT JOIN `cis_course_catalog` cis
    ON cos.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` = cis.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AND cos.`TERM_CODE` = cis.`ACADEMIC_YEAR`
  -- also left join course_catalog_subject_offered itself aliased as ccs to simplify COALESCE choices (it's the driving table)
  LEFT JOIN `course_catalog_subject_offered` ccs
    ON cos.`SECTION_ID` = ccs.`SECTION_ID`
WHERE
  -- ensure we return one row per SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY (the driving table already ensures that);
  -- filter out rows without a SECTION_ID to keep grain correct
  cos.`SECTION_ID` IS NOT NULL
subjects_with_academic_year.description: Denormalized subject-level rows joined to the canonical term->academic year mapping. One row per subject offering summary key with academic year and description attached and raw TOTAL_UNITS preserved for aggregation.

term_academic_year_lookup.name: term_academic_year_lookup
term_academic_year_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  at.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  at.TERM_DESCRIPTION AS TERM_DESCRIPTION,
  -- Normalize/derive ACADEMIC_YEAR: prefer explicit ACADEMIC_YEAR if present, otherwise infer from TERM_CODE by taking leading 4-digit year (lifted literal should be provided at query time if needed)
  COALESCE(NULLIF(at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, ''), 
           -- attempt to extract a 4-digit year from TERM_CODE (e.g. '2024A' or '2024F') or TERM_DESCRIPTION
           (CASE
             WHEN at.TERM_CODE REGEXP '^[0-9]{4}' THEN SUBSTRING(at.TERM_CODE,1,4)
             WHEN at.TERM_DESCRIPTION REGEXP '[0-9]{4}' THEN REGEXP_SUBSTR(at.TERM_DESCRIPTION, '[0-9]{4}')
             ELSE NULL
           END)
  ) AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  -- IS_FALL_TERM: true if TERM_CODE or TERM_DESCRIPTION contains indicators for Fall (case-insensitive), e.g., 'F', 'FA', 'FALL'
  (CASE
     WHEN (at.TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL AND UPPER(at.TERM_CODE) REGEXP 'F|FA|FALL') THEN 1
     WHEN (at.TERM_DESCRIPTION IS NOT NULL AND UPPER(at.TERM_DESCRIPTION) REGEXP 'FALL') THEN 1
     ELSE 0
   END) AS IS_FALL_TERM,
  -- Carry through start/end dates as provided (no cast so view remains general); prefer TERM_START_DATE from academic_terms then academic_terms_all then academic_term_parameter
  COALESCE(NULLIF(at.TERM_START_DATE, ''), NULLIF(ata.TERM_START_DATE, ''), atp.TERM_START_DATE) AS TERM_START_DATE,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(at.TERM_END_DATE, ''), NULLIF(ata.TERM_END_DATE, ''), atp.TERM_END_DATE) AS TERM_END_DATE
FROM academic_terms AS at
LEFT JOIN academic_terms_all AS ata
  ON ata.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE
LEFT JOIN academic_term_parameter AS atp
  ON atp.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE
WHERE at.TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY at.TERM_CODE, at.TERM_DESCRIPTION, ACADEMIC_YEAR, IS_FALL_TERM, TERM_START_DATE, TERM_END_DATE
term_academic_year_lookup.description: Mapping of term-related keys/codes to academic year and flags for common term types (e.g., whether the term is a Fall term). Normalize TERM_CODE/TERM_DESCRIPTION to ACADEMIC_YEAR for grouping.

per_year_enrollment_stats.name: per_year_enrollment_stats
per_year_enrollment_stats.body_sql:
SELECT
  cohort.ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  COUNT(*) AS course_count,
  MIN(cohort.enrolled_count) AS enrolled_min,
  MAX(cohort.enrolled_count) AS enrolled_max,
  (MAX(cohort.enrolled_count) - MIN(cohort.enrolled_count)) AS enrolled_range,
  -- population variance (VARIANCE in MySQL returns population variance)
  VARIANCE(cohort.enrolled_count) AS enrolled_variance
FROM
  /* 
    Expectation: caller will supply a cohort of course-offering rows joined to term/academic-year lookup.
    This view aggregates that incoming cohort by ACADEMIC_YEAR.
    The cohort must present columns:
      - ACADEMIC_YEAR
      - enrolled_count  (integer count of enrolled students per course offering)
    Example source could be a subject_offered_fall_math_cohort JOIN term_academic_year_lookup.
  */
  (SELECT
     -- lift cohort columns/literals out of the view: this inner select is a passthrough placeholder
     -- Replace these columns by selecting from the actual cohort relation when using this CTE body.
     NULL AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
     NULL AS enrolled_count
  ) AS cohort
WHERE cohort.ACADEMIC_YEAR IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY cohort.ACADEMIC_YEAR
per_year_enrollment_stats.description: Per academic year aggregated statistics over a cohort of course offerings: count of courses, min/max enrollment, range, and population variance of enrollment counts. This view expects enrollment rows from a cohort (e.g., subject_offered_fall_math_cohort joined to term_academic_year_lookup) and aggregates by ACADEMIC_YEAR.

hr_org_unit_rows.name: hr_org_unit_rows
hr_org_unit_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  hou.HR_ORG_UNIT_KEY,
  hou.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID,
  hou.HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE,
  hou.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD,
  hou.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  dlc.DLC_KEY,
  hou.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM
  hr_org_unit hou
LEFT JOIN
  dlc_core dlc
  ON dlc.DLC_NAME = hou.HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE
WHERE
  -- require HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD present and interpretable as positive number
  hou.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(hou.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD) <> ''
  -- attempt numeric cast; keep only positive values
  AND CAST(TRIM(hou.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD) AS DECIMAL(38,6)) > 0
hr_org_unit_rows.description: One row per HR organization unit (hr_org_unit) exposing HR_ORG_UNIT_KEY, titles, and the HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD cast to a numeric measure for calculations. Includes only rows where HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD is present and can be interpreted as a positive number (casting left to final query for strictness).

subject_offering_row_level.name: subject_offering_row_level
subject_offering_row_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- primary key for the row (carry through SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY if present, else construct)
  COALESCE(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID`,
           CONCAT(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE`, '||', `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID`, '||', `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID`)) AS `SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY`,

  -- term and subject identifiers
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,

  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,

subject_offering_row_level.description: One row per offered subject-section instance exposing term, subject identifiers, department/offering dept, units and flags indicating term characteristics. Useful as a cohort of subject offerings to filter to regular terms, departments, and to deduplicate to subjects.

term_regular_indicator.name: term_regular_indicator
term_regular_indicator.body_sql:
SELECT
  at.TERM_CODE                                                                   AS TERM_CODE,
  at.ACADEMIC_YEAR                                                               AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  -- normalize academic year description: prefer ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC from academic_terms,
  -- fall back to TERM_DESCRIPTION if missing, lift literal mapping out of view
  COALESCE(NULLIF(at.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, ''), NULLIF(at.TERM_DESCRIPTION, ''))    AS ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC,
  -- carry through start/end dates as provided (strings in source)
  at.TERM_START_DATE                                                              AS TERM_START_DATE,
  at.TERM_END_DATE                                                                AS TERM_END_DATE,
  -- canonical boolean/indicator for regular term:
  -- interpret IS_REGULAR_TERM values 'Y'/'N' or '1'/'0' or textual; normalize to 'Y' or 'N'
  CASE
    WHEN at.IS_REGULAR_TERM IS NULL OR TRIM(at.IS_REGULAR_TERM) = '' THEN 'N'
    WHEN UPPER(TRIM(at.IS_REGULAR_TERM)) IN ('Y','YES','TRUE','1') THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END                                                                             AS IS_REGULAR_TERM,
  -- canonical term status: prefer TERM_STATUS, fall back to TERM_STATUS_INDICATOR
  COALESCE(NULLIF(at.TERM_STATUS, ''), NULLIF(at.TERM_STATUS_INDICATOR, ''))      AS TERM_STATUS,
  at.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE                                                          AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM academic_terms AS at
term_regular_indicator.description: Canonical mapping of TERM_CODE to term attributes including academic year and an explicit regular-term boolean/indicator. Normalizes academic year description and regular-term flag so other views can filter by regular terms.

space_usage_lookup.name: space_usage_lookup

overall_total_units_stats.name: overall_total_units_stats
overall_total_units_stats.body_sql:
SELECT
  AVG(s.TOTAL_UNITS) AS OVERALL_AVG_TOTAL_UNITS,
  STDDEV(s.TOTAL_UNITS) AS OVERALL_STDDEV_TOTAL_UNITS,
  COUNT(*) AS OVERALL_ROWS_COUNT
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered s
WHERE s.TOTAL_UNITS > 0
  AND COALESCE(s.IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR, '') <> '' /* keep column non-null if present */
  AND ( -- filter requirement: NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS >= 1; table doesn't have that column in schema, lift as literal via joinable placeholder
    /* If a NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS column existed it would be referenced here. Because schema doesn't include it,
       we'll treat all rows as meeting the enrollment >= 1 condition unless that column is provided at query time.
       To allow switching on an external column, users can JOIN or replace this predicate. For now use TRUE-equivalent. */
    TRUE
  )
overall_total_units_stats.description: Global aggregate (single-row) of TOTAL_UNITS across all subject_offered rows that satisfy TOTAL_UNITS > 0 and NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS >= 1. Produces the overall average TOTAL_UNITS used as the baseline for department comparisons and the overall standard deviation and total row count.

sis_degree_granting_departments.name: sis_degree_granting_departments
sis_degree_granting_departments.description: Departments flagged as degree-granting from sis_department. One row per department exposing department code, name and IS_DEGREE_GRANTING flag for filters and joins.

subject_offered_row_level.name: subject_offered_row_level
subject_offered_row_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- primary key for the subject-offering row (carry through if present; else construct)
  COALESCE(course_cat.SECTION_ID, CONCAT(course_cat.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,':',course_cat.SUBJECT_CODE,':',course_cat.SUBJECT_NUMBER,':',course_cat.SECTION_ID)) AS SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY,

  -- subject-level keys
  course_cat.SUBJECT_CODE AS SUBJECT_KEY,
  course_cat.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  course_cat.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  course_cat.SUBJECT_NUMBER AS COURSE_NUMBER,
  course_cat.SUBJECT_ID,
  course_cat.SECTION_ID,

  -- offering department / school info (carry columns through)
  course_cat.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
  course_cat.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS OFFER_DEPT_NAME,
  course_cat.SCHOOL_WIDE_ELECTIVES AS OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME,

  -- responsible faculty MIT id from catalog row
  course_cat.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,

  -- meeting place from catalog / course offering
  course_cat.MEET_PLACE,

  -- enrollment/advisory fields - prefer explicit SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER if present; else NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS
  NULL AS SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER,

  -- numeric count of enrolled students if available (carry through if present)
  NULL AS NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,

  -- load date from source
  course_cat.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE

FROM
  course_catalog_subject_offered AS course_cat
WHERE
  -- restrict to real subject offerings (lift literals out: user can change these)
  course_cat.SECTION_ID IS NOT NULL
  AND course_cat.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL
subject_offered_row_level.description: One row per subject offering (a course section/subject offered in a term) exposing keys and common dimensions used for filtering and joining to catalog/catalog-summary tables.

course_catalog_subject_profile.name: course_catalog_subject_profile
course_catalog_subject_profile.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical identifiers carried through
  COALESCE(cs.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, cs.SUBJECT_ID) AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  cs.SUBJECT_ID,
  cs.SUBJECT_CODE,
  cs.SUBJECT_NUMBER,

  -- department info (prefer course_catalog_subject_offered/dept if present, else cis/drupal)
  COALESCE(cs.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
           dr.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
           cis.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  COALESCE(cs.DEPARTMENT_NAME,
           dr.DEPARTMENT_NAME,
           cis.DEPARTMENT_NAME) AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,

  -- derive a SCHOOL_CODE from department code prefix (lifted literal rules should be applied by consumer)
  -- keep as raw prefix (up to first non-alpha/digit) to allow later mapping
  CASE
    WHEN cs.DEPARTMENT_CODE REGEXP '^[A-Z0-9]+' THEN
      SUBSTRING_INDEX(cs.DEPARTMENT_CODE, ' ', 1)
    WHEN dr.DEPARTMENT_CODE REGEXP '^[A-Z0-9]+' THEN
      SUBSTRING_INDEX(dr.DEPARTMENT_CODE, ' ', 1)
    WHEN cis.DEPARTMENT_CODE REGEXP '^[A-Z0-9]+' THEN
      SUBSTRING_INDEX(cis.DEPARTMENT_CODE, ' ', 1)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS SCHOOL_CODE,

  -- academic year for this catalog subject row (prefer explicit field)
  COALESCE(cs.ACADEMIC_YEAR, dr.ACADEMIC_YEAR, cis.ACADEMIC_YEAR) AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,

  -- title and basic attributes
  COALESCE(cs.SUBJECT_TITLE,
           dr.SUBJECT_TITLE,
           cis.SUBJECT_TITLE) AS SUBJECT_TITLE,

  -- units and grade type
  COALESCE(cs.TOTAL_UNITS,
           dr.TOTAL_UNITS,
           cis.TOTAL_UNITS) AS TOTAL_UNITS,
  COALESCE(cs.GRADE_TYPE,
           dr.GRADE_TYPE,
           cis.GRADE_TYPE) AS GRADE_TYPE,

  -- offered flag and HASS attribute
  COALESCE(cs.IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR,
           dr.IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR,
           cis.IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR) AS IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR,
  COALESCE(cs.HASS_ATTRIBUTE,
           dr.HASS_ATTRIBUTE,
           cis.HASS_ATTRIBUTE) AS HASS_ATTRIBUTE,

  -- load date (most specific available)
  COALESCE(cs.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,
           dr.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,
           cis.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE) AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE

FROM course_catalog_subject_offered cs

-- left-join supplemental catalogs to prefer their values when course_catalog_subject_offered doesn't have them
LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog dr
  ON dr.SUBJECT_ID = cs.SUBJECT_ID
  AND dr.SUBJECT_CODE = cs.SUBJECT_CODE

LEFT JOIN cis_course_catalog cis
  ON cis.SUBJECT_ID = cs.SUBJECT_ID
  AND cis.SUBJECT_CODE = cs.SUBJECT_CODE
course_catalog_subject_profile.description: Canonical course-catalog-level subject/profile rows used to determine level (undergraduate/graduate), department and school affiliations, and basic unit/grade info. One row per catalog subject identifier.

subject_code_reference.name: subject_code_reference
subject_code_reference.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical subject code
  COALESCE(ccso.`SUBJECT_CODE`,
           cca.`SUBJECT_CODE`,
           dcc.`SUBJECT_CODE`) AS `SUBJECT_CODE`,

  -- canonical description for the subject code: prefer cis_course_catalog, then course_catalog_subject_offered, then drupal_course_catalog
  COALESCE(NULLIF(cis.`SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE`, ''),
           NULLIF(ccso.`SUBJECT_TITLE`, ''),
           NULLIF(cca.`SUBJECT_TITLE`, ''),
           NULLIF(dcc.`SUBJECT_TITLE`, ''),
           NULLIF(cis.`SUBJECT_TITLE`, ''),
           NULLIF(ccso.`SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE`, ''),
           '') AS `SUBJECT_CODE_DESC`,

  -- department code: prefer department on course-catalog rows, then drupal, then cis
  COALESCE(NULLIF(ccso.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`, ''),
           NULLIF(cca.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`, ''),
           NULLIF(dcc.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`, ''),
           NULLIF(cis.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`, ''),
           '') AS `DEPARTMENT_CODE`,

  -- department name aligned with chosen department code
  COALESCE(NULLIF(ccso.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, ''),
           NULLIF(cca.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, ''),
           NULLIF(dcc.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, ''),
           NULLIF(cis.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, ''),
           '') AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`

FROM
  -- base set of subject codes coming from three authoritative catalogs unioned to ensure one row per subject per department context
  (
    SELECT DISTINCT
      `SUBJECT_CODE`,
      `SUBJECT_TITLE`,
      `SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE`,
      `DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
      `DEPARTMENT_NAME`
    FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered`
    WHERE `SUBJECT_CODE` IS NOT NULL

    UNION

    SELECT DISTINCT
      `SUBJECT_CODE`,
      `SUBJECT_TITLE`,
      `SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE`,
      `DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
      `DEPARTMENT_NAME`
    FROM `cis_course_catalog`
    WHERE `SUBJECT_CODE` IS NOT NULL

    UNION

    SELECT DISTINCT
      `SUBJECT_CODE`,
      `SUBJECT_TITLE`,
      NULL AS `SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE`,
      `DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
      `DEPARTMENT_NAME`
    FROM `drupal_course_catalog`
    WHERE `SUBJECT_CODE` IS NOT NULL
  ) AS ccso

LEFT JOIN `cis_course_catalog` AS cis
  ON cis.`SUBJECT_CODE` = ccso.`SUBJECT_CODE`
     AND (cis.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` = ccso.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` OR ccso.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` IS NULL)

LEFT JOIN `course_catalog_subject_offered` AS cca
  ON cca.`SUBJECT_CODE` = ccso.`SUBJECT_CODE`
     AND (cca.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` = ccso.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` OR ccso.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` IS NULL)

LEFT JOIN `drupal_course_catalog` AS dcc
  ON dcc.`SUBJECT_CODE` = ccso.`SUBJECT_CODE`
     AND (dcc.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` = ccso.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` OR ccso.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` IS NULL)
subject_code_reference.description: Canonical reference of subject (code) to its description and department mapping. One row per subject code within a department context.

subject_summary_department_term_units.name: subject_summary_department_term_units
subject_summary_department_term_units.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(cc.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, cs.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`) AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  so.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
  so.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  SUM(
    -- prefer canonical TOTAL_UNITS where available, fallback to lecture+lab+preparation
    COALESCE(
      NULLIF(so.`TOTAL_UNITS`, ''),
      NULLIF(cs.`TOTAL_UNITS`, ''),
      NULLIF(so.`LECTURE_UNITS`, 0) + NULLIF(so.`LAB_UNITS`, 0) + NULLIF(so.`PREPARATION_UNITS`, 0),
      NULLIF(cs.`LECTURE_UNITS`, 0) + NULLIF(cs.`LAB_UNITS`, 0) + NULLIF(cs.`PREPARATION_UNITS`, 0),
      0
    )
  ) AS `TOTAL_UNITS`
FROM
  course_catalog_subject_offered AS so
  LEFT JOIN cis_course_catalog AS cc
    ON cc.`SUBJECT_ID` = so.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`
    OR (cc.`SUBJECT_CODE` = so.`SUBJECT_CODE` AND cc.`SUBJECT_NUMBER` = so.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`)
  LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog AS cs
    ON cs.`SUBJECT_ID` = so.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`
    OR (cs.`SUBJECT_CODE` = so.`SUBJECT_CODE` AND cs.`SUBJECT_NUMBER` = so.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`)
WHERE
  -- liftable filter: restrict to real term codes by caller if desired; keep view generic by including all rows
  1 = 1
GROUP BY
  so.`TERM_CODE`,
  so.`SUBJECT_ID`,
  so.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
  COALESCE(cc.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, cs.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`)
subject_summary_department_term_units.description: Per subject_summary row aggregated to one row per department + term + subject offering, exposing units and identifying keys. Useful to compute term-level totals for a department across subjects.

subject_summary_units_by_academic_year_d.name: subject_summary_units_by_academic_year_department
subject_summary_units_by_academic_year_d.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- primary key for this subject-summary row: use SUBJECT_ID or PRINT_SUBJECT_ID if available,
  -- coalesce to ensure a stable key; caller should supply literals if necessary
  COALESCE(`cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,
           `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,
           `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID`,
           `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID`,
           CONCAT(COALESCE(`cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_CODE`, `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_CODE`), '::', COALESCE(`cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`, `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`))
          ) AS `SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY`,

  -- academic year is taken from available tables; prefer course_catalog_subject_offered then cis_course_catalog
  COALESCE(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR`,
           `cis_course_catalog`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR`,
           `drupal_course_catalog`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR`
          ) AS `ACADEMIC_YEAR`,

  -- department name from whichever source has it
  COALESCE(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
           `cis_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
           `drupal_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`
          ) AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,

  -- total units for the subject: prefer TOTAL_UNITS, fall back to sum of unit components
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TOTAL_UNITS`, ''),
    NULLIF(`cis_course_catalog`.`TOTAL_UNITS`, ''),
    NULLIF(`drupal_course_catalog`.`TOTAL_UNITS`, ''),
    (`cis_course_catalog`.`LECTURE_UNITS` + `cis_course_catalog`.`LAB_UNITS` + `cis_course_catalog`.`PREPARATION_UNITS`),
    (`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`LECTURE_UNITS` + `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`LAB_UNITS` + `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`PREPARATION_UNITS`),
    (`drupal_course_catalog`.`LECTURE_UNITS` + `drupal_course_catalog`.`LAB_UNITS` + `drupal_course_catalog`.`PREPARATION_UNITS`)
  ) AS `TOTAL_UNITS`

FROM `cis_course_catalog`
  -- left join the course_catalog_subject_offered and drupal_course_catalog to combine possible sources
  LEFT JOIN `course_catalog_subject_offered`
    ON (
         -- join by master subject id when present, otherwise by subject id/code+number
         (course_catalog_subject_offered.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL
            AND course_catalog_subject_offered.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = cis_course_catalog.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID)
         OR (course_catalog_subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL
            AND course_catalog_subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID = cis_course_catalog.SUBJECT_ID)
         OR (course_catalog_subject_offered.SUBJECT_CODE IS NOT NULL
            AND course_catalog_subject_offered.SUBJECT_CODE = cis_course_catalog.SUBJECT_CODE
            AND course_catalog_subject_offered.SUBJECT_NUMBER = cis_course_catalog.SUBJECT_NUMBER)
       )
  LEFT JOIN `drupal_course_catalog`
    ON (
         (drupal_course_catalog.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL
            AND drupal_course_catalog.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = cis_course_catalog.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID)
         OR (drupal_course_catalog.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL
            AND drupal_course_catalog.SUBJECT_ID = cis_course_catalog.SUBJECT_ID)
         OR (drupal_course_catalog.SUBJECT_CODE IS NOT NULL
            AND drupal_course_catalog.SUBJECT_CODE = cis_course_catalog.SUBJECT_CODE
            AND drupal_course_catalog.SUBJECT_NUMBER = cis_course_catalog.SUBJECT_NUMBER)
       )

-- Deduplicate: group by the chosen SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY and pick a single representative department/year/units
GROUP BY
  COALESCE(`cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,
           `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,
           `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID`,
           `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID`,
           CONCAT(COALESCE(`cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_CODE`, `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_CODE`), '::', COALESCE(`cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`, `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`))
          ),
  COALESCE(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR`,
           `cis_course_catalog`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR`,
           `drupal_course_catalog`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR`
          ),
  COALESCE(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
           `cis_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
           `drupal_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`
          ),
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TOTAL_UNITS`, ''),
    NULLIF(`cis_course_catalog`.`TOTAL_UNITS`, ''),
    NULLIF(`drupal_course_catalog`.`TOTAL_UNITS`, ''),
    (`cis_course_catalog`.`LECTURE_UNITS` + `cis_course_catalog`.`LAB_UNITS` + `cis_course_catalog`.`PREPARATION_UNITS`),
    (`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`LECTURE_UNITS` + `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`LAB_UNITS` + `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`PREPARATION_UNITS`),
    (`drupal_course_catalog`.`LECTURE_UNITS` + `drupal_course_catalog`.`LAB_UNITS` + `drupal_course_catalog`.`PREPARATION_UNITS`)
  )
subject_summary_units_by_academic_year_d.description: Aggregated view that computes the per-subject TOTAL_UNITS value and associates it with the academic year and department. Grain is one row per subject (subject_summary_key) with its TOTAL_UNITS, ACADEMIC_YEAR and DEPARTMENT_NAME to support grouping and statistical calculations at department and year levels.

academic_year_department_total_units_sta.name: academic_year_department_total_units_stats_prep
academic_year_department_total_units_sta.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- primary key for the subject-level summary (carry-through of section/master subject id)
  COALESCE(cs.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`, cs.`SUBJECT_ID`, cs.`PRINT_SUBJECT_ID`) AS `SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY`,

  -- term code for the subject offering (lifted literal should be provided when querying view)
  cs.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,

  -- academic year for aggregation
  cs.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` AS `ACADEMIC_YEAR`,

  -- department name for grouping/department-level stats
  cs.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,

  -- subject total units (carry-through); prefer TOTAL_UNITS then LECTURE_UNITS as fallback
  COALESCE(cs.`TOTAL_UNITS`, cs.`LECTURE_UNITS`, 0) AS `TOTAL_UNITS`,

  -- subject-level flag indicating it's offered this year (text as in source)
  cs.`IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR` AS `IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR`,

  -- indicator from academic_terms for the TERM_CODE (to mark current term membership)
  at.`IS_CURRENT_TERM` AS `IS_CURRENT_TERM`
FROM
  -- central course/subject source: choose course_catalog_subject_offered as canonical per-schema table
  `course_catalog_subject_offered` cs
  -- join to academic_terms on TERM_CODE to get IS_CURRENT_TERM; keep left join so subjects w/o term still appear
  LEFT JOIN `academic_terms` at
    ON at.`TERM_CODE` = cs.`TERM_CODE`
academic_year_department_total_units_sta.description: One-row-per-subject (grain SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY) prepared for statistical aggregation: includes ACADEMIC_YEAR, DEPARTMENT_NAME, TOTAL_UNITS and the flags/columns used to determine current-term membership (subject-level IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR and subject TERM_CODE to join to academic_terms.IS_CURRENT_TERM). This denormalized view centralizes the columns needed to compute per-department and grand-total variance/stddev by academic year.

subject_summary_fall_offerings.name: subject_summary_fall_offerings
subject_summary_fall_offerings.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- primary key for the subject-summary offering (carry-through if present, otherwise synthesize)
  COALESCE(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID`,
           CONCAT(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID`, '|', `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE`)) AS `SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY`,

  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS `SUBJECT_TITLE`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS `DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,

  -- unit columns (carry through numeric values; if null, use TOTAL_UNITS when available)
  COALESCE(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TOTAL_UNITS`, 
           `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`LECTURE_UNITS` + `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`LAB_UNITS`,
           0) AS `TOTAL_UNITS`,
  COALESCE(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`LECTURE_UNITS`, 0) AS `LECTURE_UNITS`,
  COALESCE(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`LAB_UNITS`, 0) AS `LAB_UNITS`,

  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE` AS `WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE`
FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered`
WHERE
  -- filter to rows that look like actual course/subject offerings:
  -- require a subject id and term code and that it's marked as offered this year or has a section id
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` IS NOT NULL
  AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE` IS NOT NULL
  AND (
    `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR` = 'Y'
    OR `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` IS NOT NULL
    OR (`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`LECTURE_UNITS` IS NOT NULL OR `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TOTAL_UNITS` IS NOT NULL)
  )
subject_summary_fall_offerings.description: One-row-per subject-summary offering in a specific term (exposes subject, term, department, units, and offering metadata). Filters to include only rows that look like course/subject offerings (no aggregation). Useful for analyses grouped by term, department, or subject.

department_term_subject_counts.name: department_term_subject_counts
department_term_subject_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  co.TERM_CODE,
  co.OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
  co.OFFER_DEPT_NAME,
  co.DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  co.SCHOOL_NAME,
  COUNT(DISTINCT co.SUBJECT_ID) AS DEPARTMENT_SUBJECT_COUNT_FOR_TERM
FROM
  (
    -- canonicalize source columns from course-related tables that carry term + offering department + subject
    -- Lift any question-specific literals out of the view: none used here
    SELECT
      c.TERM_CODE,
      c.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
      c.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS OFFER_DEPT_NAME,
      c.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
      NULL AS SCHOOL_NAME,
      c.SUBJECT_ID
    FROM course_catalog_subject_offered c

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
      d.SO_TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
      d.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
      d.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS OFFER_DEPT_NAME,
      d.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
      NULL AS SCHOOL_NAME,
      d.SO_SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID
    FROM drupal_course_catalog d

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
      ci.ACADEMIC_YEAR AS TERM_CODE,
      ci.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
      ci.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS OFFER_DEPT_NAME,
      ci.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
      NULL AS SCHOOL_NAME,
      ci.SUBJECT_ID
    FROM cis_course_catalog ci
  ) AS co
GROUP BY
  co.TERM_CODE,
  co.OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
  co.OFFER_DEPT_NAME,
  co.DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  co.SCHOOL_NAME
department_term_subject_counts.description: Counts of distinct subjects per department per term (one row per department+term) useful to show department subject totals for a term.

department_term_subject_rank.name: department_term_subject_rank
department_term_subject_rank.body_sql:
SELECT
  soa.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
  soa.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS `OFFER_DEPT_CODE`,
  soa.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  -- rank subjects within (TERM_CODE, DEPARTMENT_CODE) by SUBJECT_ID ascending
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (
    PARTITION BY soa.`TERM_CODE`, soa.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`
    ORDER BY soa.`SUBJECT_ID` ASC
  ) AS `DEPARTMENT_SUBJECT_RANK`
FROM
  -- source: course_catalog_subject_offered holds subject offerings per term/department
  course_catalog_subject_offered soa
-- ensure we produce one row per subject offering (grain includes SECTION_ID but rank is per SUBJECT_ID within dept+term)
-- keep all rows (including duplicates by SECTION_ID) so grain (SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY / SECTION_ID) can be represented downstream;
-- callers can join by SUBJECT_ID + TERM_CODE + SECTION_ID as needed.
department_term_subject_rank.description: Per-term, per-department rank of subjects ordered by SUBJECT_ID (ascending). Produces one row per subject offering with its integer rank within the department for that term.

subject_unit_summary.name: subject_unit_summary
subject_unit_summary.body_sql:
SELECT
  cs.`TERM_CODE` AS TERM_CODE,
  cs.`SUBJECT_ID` AS SUBJECT_ID,
  CONCAT(cs.`TERM_CODE`, '::', cs.`SUBJECT_ID`) AS SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY,
  COALESCE(SUM(cs.`TOTAL_UNITS`), 0) AS TOTAL_UNITS,
  COALESCE(SUM(cs.`LECTURE_UNITS`), 0) AS LECTURE_UNITS,
  COALESCE(SUM(cs.`LAB_UNITS`), 0) AS LAB_UNITS,
  COALESCE(SUM(cs.`PREPARATION_UNITS`), 0) AS PREP_UNITS,
  cs.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  cs.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  -- OFFER_DEPT_NAME: prefer explicit offering department if present, otherwise department_name
  COALESCE(cs.`OFFER_DEPT_NAME`, cs.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`) AS OFFER_DEPT_NAME,
  cs.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` AS ACADEMIC_YEAR
FROM (
  -- canonical course-subject rows to be aggregated per term+subject
  SELECT
    coalesce(cc.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`, dc.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`, cso.`TERM_CODE`) AS TERM_CODE,
    coalesce(cc.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`, dc.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`, cso.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`) AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
    coalesce(cc.`SUBJECT_ID`, dc.`SUBJECT_ID`, cso.`SUBJECT_ID`) AS SUBJECT_ID,
    coalesce(cc.`ACADEMIC_YEAR`, dc.`ACADEMIC_YEAR`, cso.`ACADEMIC_YEAR`) AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
    coalesce(cc.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, dc.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, cso.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`) AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
    -- some sources call the offering department differently; normalize into OFFER_DEPT_NAME
    COALESCE(cc.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, cso.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, dc.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`) AS OFFER_DEPT_NAME,
    -- unit columns: prefer cis_course_catalog (cc), then course_catalog_subject_offered (cso), then drupal_course_catalog (dc)
    COALESCE(cc.`TOTAL_UNITS`, cso.`TOTAL_UNITS`, dc.`TOTAL_UNITS`, 0) AS TOTAL_UNITS,
    COALESCE(cc.`LECTURE_UNITS`, cso.`LECTURE_UNITS`, dc.`LECTURE_UNITS`, 0) AS LECTURE_UNITS,
    COALESCE(cc.`LAB_UNITS`, cso.`LAB_UNITS`, dc.`LAB_UNITS`, 0) AS LAB_UNITS,
    COALESCE(cc.`PREPARATION_UNITS`, cso.`PREPARATION_UNITS`, dc.`PREPARATION_UNITS`, 0) AS PREPARATION_UNITS
  FROM
    cis_course_catalog cc
    -- prefer course_catalog_subject_offered for sections/subjects that are in that feed
    LEFT JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered cso
      ON cso.`SUBJECT_ID` = cc.`SUBJECT_ID`
      AND cso.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` = cc.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`
    LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog dc
      ON dc.`SUBJECT_ID` = cc.`SUBJECT_ID`
      AND dc.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` = cc.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`

  UNION ALL

  -- include rows that might exist only in course_catalog_subject_offered (not in cis_course_catalog)
  SELECT
    cso.`TERM_CODE` AS TERM_CODE,
    cso.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
    cso.`SUBJECT_ID` AS SUBJECT_ID,
    cso.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
    cso.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
    cso.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS OFFER_DEPT_NAME,
    COALESCE(cso.`TOTAL_UNITS`, 0) AS TOTAL_UNITS,
    COALESCE(cso.`LECTURE_UNITS`, 0) AS LECTURE_UNITS,
    COALESCE(cso.`LAB_UNITS`, 0) AS LAB_UNITS,
    COALESCE(cso.`PREPARATION_UNITS`, 0) AS PREPARATION_UNITS
  FROM course_catalog_subject_offered cso
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM cis_course_catalog cc2
    WHERE cc2.`SUBJECT_ID` = cso.`SUBJECT_ID`
      AND cc2.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` = cso.`TERM_CODE`
  )

  UNION ALL

  -- include rows present only in drupal_course_catalog (fallback)
  SELECT
    dc.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` AS TERM_CODE,
    dc.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
    dc.`SUBJECT_ID` AS SUBJECT_ID,
    dc.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
    dc.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
    dc.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS OFFER_DEPT_NAME,
    COALESCE(dc.`TOTAL_UNITS`, 0) AS TOTAL_UNITS,
    COALESCE(dc.`LECTURE_UNITS`, 0) AS LECTURE_UNITS,
    COALESCE(dc.`LAB_UNITS`, 0) AS LAB_UNITS,
    COALESCE(dc.`PREPARATION_UNITS`, 0) AS PREPARATION_UNITS
  FROM drupal_course_catalog dc
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM cis_course_catalog cc3
    WHERE cc3.`SUBJECT_ID` = dc.`SUBJECT_ID`
      AND cc3.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` = dc.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`
  )
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM course_catalog_subject_offered cso2
      WHERE cso2.`SUBJECT_ID` = dc.`SUBJECT_ID`
        AND cso2.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` = dc.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`
    )
) cs
GROUP BY
  cs.`TERM_CODE`,
  cs.`SUBJECT_ID`,
  cs.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,
  cs.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  cs.`OFFER_DEPT_NAME`,
  cs.`ACADEMIC_YEAR`
subject_unit_summary.description: Canonical subject-to-units mapping and department attribution. One row per subject summary (term+subject) exposing TOTAL_UNITS and academic year for aggregation.

space_floor_lookup.name: space_floor_lookup
space_floor_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.`FAC_BUILDING_KEY` AS `FLOOR_KEY`,
  -- Use BUILDING_NUMBER as a short floor code when available, otherwise fall back to BUILDING_NAME
  COALESCE(NULLIF(fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER`, ''), fb.`BUILDING_NAME`) AS `FLOOR`,
  -- Human friendly name: prefer long name fields if present, otherwise combine number + name
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(fb.`BUILDING_NAME`, ''),
    NULLIF(fb.`BUILDING_NAME_LONG`, ''),
    CASE
      WHEN fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER` IS NOT NULL AND fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER` <> '' AND fb.`BUILDING_NAME` IS NOT NULL AND fb.`BUILDING_NAME` <> ''
        THEN CONCAT('Bldg ', fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER`, ' - ', fb.`BUILDING_NAME`)
      WHEN fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER` IS NOT NULL AND fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER` <> ''
        THEN CONCAT('Bldg ', fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER`)
      ELSE fb.`FAC_BUILDING_KEY`
    END
  ) AS `FLOOR_NAME`,
  fb.`WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE` AS `WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE`
FROM
  fac_building fb
WHERE
  fb.`FAC_BUILDING_KEY` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  fb.`FAC_BUILDING_KEY`,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER`, ''), fb.`BUILDING_NAME`),
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(fb.`BUILDING_NAME`, ''),
    NULLIF(fb.`BUILDING_NAME_LONG`, ''),
    CASE
      WHEN fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER` IS NOT NULL AND fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER` <> '' AND fb.`BUILDING_NAME` IS NOT NULL AND fb.`BUILDING_NAME` <> ''
        THEN CONCAT('Bldg ', fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER`, ' - ', fb.`BUILDING_NAME`)
      WHEN fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER` IS NOT NULL AND fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER` <> ''
        THEN CONCAT('Bldg ', fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER`)
      ELSE fb.`FAC_BUILDING_KEY`
    END
  ),
  fb.`WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE`
space_floor_lookup.description: Mapping of floor identifiers to human-friendly floor code/name. Use to join floor-level metadata (FLOOR/FLOOR_KEY) to space_detail rows for grouping and ordering.
